findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log with a Matrix coherence preflight row
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so this plan PR carries no `Document Quality Gate` log at all. REVIEW.md requires a current log in the description; because `## Decision-gate matrix (plan-time classification)` is a stateful contract, that log must also carry a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned `Not applicable`. A missing log is at minimum an important finding, and the absent preflight row for a plan that actually contains a decision matrix is blocking before `ready-for-human-review`. Add the log and the preflight row.

findings.title: Record the plan-authoring-rigor per-rule outcomes
findings.body: The plan carries no plan-authoring-rigor outcome record. REVIEW.md requires the plan's per-rule record (the six canonical rules, each `Satisfied` / `Not applicable` / `Unsatisfied`, with evidence at the recorded revision and a rationale for any `Not applicable`). Nothing here records which rules fired or why not, and Group H treats a missing outcome record as blocking. Add the six rule lines with the `def04bd` evidence references.

findings.title: Resolve where the AC17 statement is recorded
findings.body: `## Documentation Updates` says AC17's statement `belongs in docs/testing/ronda/sweep-effect-evidence.md` (and step 14 sends it there), but the smoke runbook's Step 12 opens `docs/testing/ronda/sweep-real-pr-evidence.md` and requires that document to state the seeded benchmark is not a regression gate until the AC12/AC13 seeds exist and that the restored gate's pass/fail contract is deferred. An implementer following the plan fails the runbook's own assertion. Pick one home (or require both) and align step 14 and smoke Step 12.

findings.title: Make the AC14 credential scan consistent with the AC13 seed
findings.body: Scenario 7 says the test walks every seed and every committed evidence/fixture file under the benchmark tree and under `docs/testing/ronda/`, and fails if any value matches a real-credential shape (`sk-...`, `ghp_...`, a Bearer authorization value, or a token/password/secret/api-key field carrying a non-placeholder value), while the same sentence exempts values declared in the manifest as non-functional. The shape scan never consults that declaration, so the AC13 seed added on line 152 (credential-shaped by requirement, possibly a `forbiddenValue`) trips the scan, and scanning all of `docs/testing/ronda/` also reaches prose that legitimately names tokens or authorization. Define the exemption mechanism (for example a declared placeholder allowlist scoped to the benchmark fixture tree) and assert AC14's real-vs-non-functional distinction rather than prefix shape alone.

findings.title: Give the pass a way to reach the loadSweepList path seam
findings.body: `src/review/sweep-categories.ts` exposes its optional `path` only as the test seam, and production `run-review-pass.ts` is shown calling `loadSweepList()` with no argument (Code Samples, lines 195-196). Yet scenario 5 and smoke Step 4 require the pass-orchestration suite to drive the malformed-list and unrecognized-enablement branches end to end through the same seam. With no injection point on the pass, those tests cannot supply a malformed list without unplanned module or filesystem mocking, which the plan neither specifies nor verifies. State the mechanism in step 8 (for example a `deps.loadSweepList` seam or a pass-level options path) and use it in the tests.

findings.title: Define how the version-attestation basis reaches the run record
findings.body: The benchmark `configuration` block must carry an operator-recorded version-attestation basis, but no input is defined for it: the only new flags are `--sweep-mode`, `--runs`, and `--output-file`, and no config key is named. Step 11 and smoke Step 8 simultaneously require the evidence to be assembled from run outputs with `no run is hand-transcribed`, which leaves manual JSON editing as the only route and makes the attestation unverifiable. Add the flag or config key that supplies the attestation for a run set and say when it is recorded.

findings.title: Carry category attribution outside the published finding text
findings.body: The `src/inference/review-prompt.ts` entry tells the model that a finding in a swept category must name that category's identifier in its own `title` or `body`, and the classifier reads that text. The finding body is the published review body, where the spec keeps category information off the review (AC1: no per-category record in the published review body; Operational Visibility: findings published exactly as in a non-sweep review, with attribution on the record surfaces). The approach also makes AC1's per-category outcomes and AC15(d) membership depend on unenforced model compliance: a genuine category finding the model does not label is recorded as `produced_none` plus `uncategorized`. Carry attribution on an internal channel (for example a response field stripped before publication) or a deterministic match that does not require the model to print the identifier, and reconcile the review-body question with the spec before implementation.

findings.title: Fix stale Implementation Order step references
findings.body: The `src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts` entry says the new CLI flags are specified in Implementation Order step 10, but the flags are step 11 (step 10 is the fixture seeds). Step 11 itself says `The evidence doc (step 11) is assembled from those files` (line 225), although the evidence campaign is step 12. Both references are stale and send a reader to the wrong step; renumber them.

findings.title: Verify the code and CLI references the plan relies on
findings.body: Step 6 and the `model-client.ts` entry rely on exact source positions (`src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts:447-449`, `:475-489`, `src/cli/review-pr.ts` L81-90, `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` L224-233, test lines L26/L243/L111/L1104/L1434/L1502/L1634) and on the completeness claim that the three `ModelClient`-referencing test files are the complete set per `grep -rl ModelClient tests/`; the campaign commands also treat `--manifest`, `--patches`, `--quality`, and `--precision-response-file` as existing options. None of this appears in the Verification Log (which records only the benchmark functions and `benchmark:quality`), so the counts, line numbers, and flag semantics cannot be checked against the codebase, including what `--quality` changes since smoke Step 8's recall commands omit it while Step 9 adds it. Add Verification Log rows with the actual command output, or mark the claims unverified for the implementer to confirm.

findings.title: Schedule the AC6/AC7 list-content assertions after the test file exists
findings.body: Step 2 requires the AC6/AC7 assertions of Testing Strategy scenario 8 to pass against the new JSON, but scenario 8 places those assertions in the new `tests/unit/review/sweep-categories.test.ts`, which step 4 creates (and step 4 schedules only scenario 2's cases). As ordered, step 2's verification cannot run and the content assertions have no scheduled author. Move the AC6/AC7 assertions into step 4 or a step after it, and keep step 2's verification to parsing and the counting-unit statement.

findings.title: Add the Plan Authoring Rigor per-rule outcome record
findings.body: The plan has no per-rule outcome record for the six plan-authoring-rigor rules (Sampling an external output distribution; One normative statement per fact; Counts of codebase artifacts; Independent verification of existence claims; Expectations at the composed call site; A conditional obligation names its scope), no `Satisfied`/`Not applicable`/`Unsatisfied` outcome labels, and no recorded revision SHA for re-runnable evidence. REVIEW.md's Plan authoring rigor backstop treats a missing outcome record or a missing `Not applicable` rationale as blocking per Group H, and evidence recorded only in PR comments is likewise blocking. Add the record to the plan (beside the Verification Log) with each rule's trigger, outcome, and repository-derived evidence at `def04bd`.

findings.title: Supply the Document Quality Gate log, including the Matrix coherence preflight row
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required `Document Quality Gate` log is absent; REVIEW.md makes a missing log important by default. The plan also contains stateful contracts (the Decision-gate matrix and the enablement precedence rules), so the log must carry a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned `Not applicable`. Leaving the row out, or later recording `Not applicable — no stateful contract`, would be a blocking misclassification because the plan does contain one.

findings.title: Flag the degraded-record boundary as an interpretation of AC1, not a settled rule
findings.body: Step 1 asserts that AC1's terminal-failure rule 'draws the line at the review request the pass issued' and that a pass dying between `readChangedFiles` and `deps.model.complete` 'owes no sweep record at all, not even a degraded one'. AC1 itself classifies 'a model or GitHub error raised after the changed files are read' as a pass that reaches review execution and then fails terminally, and AC18/AC19 key the unrecognized-enablement and `sweep-did-not-run` records to 'a pass that reaches review execution'. The narrowing is defensible only if AC1's definition (reads the changed files and runs the review) governs over that parenthetical; state that reading as an assumption the implementer must confirm, or plan the degraded record for the read-to-request window. Testing Strategy scenario 5 and runbook Step 5 currently encode the narrower reading as settled behavior.

findings.title: Reconcile the identifier-in-finding-text instruction with the unchanged output contract
findings.body: The prompt section requires a finding in a swept category to 'name that category's identifier in its own `title` or `body` text', while the same bullet says this 'changes no part of the output contract'. It does change what the published review body contains: internal category tokens become part of reviewer-visible finding text, and the spec's Out of Scope list keeps the review output contract unchanged apart from the summary statement and the pass records (AC1, AC3). Either justify the instruction against that restriction (identifiers are not display labels, so AC3's display-label rule is not the whole story) or derive attribution without model-authored tokens.

findings.title: Mark the five-category enumeration as binding
findings.body: The recorded-artifact bullet enumerates the five swept categories, and Testing Strategy scenario 8 asserts 'exactly the five required categories', so the enumeration is intended as binding, but it carries no literal `**Binding enumeration**` marker. REVIEW.md makes an unmarked enumeration indicative and satisfiable by a coverage-equivalent set at implementation time. Add the marker on or immediately above the line that introduces it, or drop the exactness assertion.

findings.title: Validate that `matchTerms` are lowercase
findings.body: The artifact defines `matchTerms` as 'lowercase literal substrings' and `classifyFindings` lowercases finding text before substring matching, but the AC19 validation list requires only 'non-empty array of non-blank strings'. A mixed-case term passes validation and silently never matches. Require normalized lowercase terms in the validator (or normalize both sides) so the list cannot validate into a non-matching state.

findings.title: Use one name for the classifier terms and the fixture match groups
findings.body: `matchTerms` is defined as the sweep category-list classifier field (lowercase literals matched against finding text). The state-reconstruction seed row then uses 'matchTerms over head, api, evidence/inference' for the fixture seed, while Implementation Order step 10 calls the manifest's structure the 'legacy `matchTermGroups` shape'. Two different structures now share one name, and the slash form is ambiguous for a literal list. Name the manifest structure explicitly (e.g. `matchTermGroups`) and state which structure the new seeds extend.

findings.title: Give each new seed an exact target path
findings.body: All five new seeds are specified as '(path `src/benchmark/git-history.ts` or similar)' and equivalents. Seed patches must name concrete paths, so 'or similar' forces the implementer to guess and makes the fixture's content identity depend on an unstated choice; the Verification Log also never confirms that `src/benchmark/` exists. State the exact path per seed (creating the directory if intended) so the seed work is executable without judgment.

findings.title: Correct the snapshot ordering reference to step 10
findings.body: The original-thirteen snapshot row says the copy happens 'before step 9 mutates the live fixture', but step 9 is the workflow and example-config step; the live fixture is mutated in step 10 ('first snapshot the pre-extension fixture ... then add the five seeds'). Fix the step reference so the snapshot ordering is unambiguous.

findings.title: Schedule the `RondaConfig` literal updates required by step 1
findings.body: Step 1 makes `sweepMode`/`sweepModeRaw` required fields, and the Backend/API section says the two `loadConfig` catch-block fallbacks (`src/cli/review-pr.ts` L81-90, `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` L224-233) and the test config literals (`tests/unit/core/run-review-pass.test.ts` `createConfig`, `tests/integration/review-pass.test.ts` L84/L223/L304) must gain them or `npm run typecheck` fails. No Implementation Order step performs or verifies those edits, and step 1 verifies only `tests/unit/config/load-config.test.ts`. Add the literal updates to step 1 (or their own step) with an `npm run typecheck` check.

findings.title: `--runs` default cannot keep today's output identical
findings.body: The `--runs` bullet says 'Default 1 keeps today's single-run output identical', but the same step makes every run record carry the new `fixture` and `configuration` identity blocks plus per-pass cost fields, and the output-shape bullet states both blocks are present on every run of both arms. Either the default output changes or the blocks are conditional; say which, and update any test that assumes byte-identical default output.

findings.title: Confirm the `--manifest` and `--patches` flags the campaign depends on
findings.body: Step 11 adds exactly three flags (`--sweep-mode`, `--runs`, `--output-file`), yet the campaign legs, the `fixture` block, and smoke-test Step 8 invoke `--manifest` and `--patches` (and rely on `--quality` and `--precision-response-file`). The Verification Log's benchmark-runner row confirms only `runRecallBenchmark`/`runPrecisionFixture` and `npm run benchmark:quality`, not those flags. Confirm them against `src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts` and record it, or add them in step 11; otherwise the original-thirteen control cannot be run as written.

findings.title: Record the AC9 per-configuration precision fields, not just the verdict
findings.body: AC9 requires the evidence to report unexpected findings per configuration, the attribution for sweep-on findings (and sweep-off findings reported as unattributed), whether each precision fixture stayed clean in each configuration, and the regression result. Step 12 lists only 'the precision regression result under the strict no-tolerance test'. Runbook Step 9 reads counts and per-fixture clean status but its expected result does not require recording them. Add those AC9 fields to step 12's evidence list and the runbook's expected result.

findings.title: Add the list-revision outcomes the spec's tier row states
findings.body: The plan's Evidence-tier transition row says only 'all other combinations unchanged', but the spec's matrix row states two more outcomes explicitly: `fixture_only` on a list revision stays `fixture_only`, and `real_pr_provisional` on a list revision stays `real_pr_provisional` with the counted pull requests restarting at zero. The plan says the implementation's records must reproduce these rows exactly, so the missing count-restart outcome is a reproducibility gap; add both outcomes to the row.

findings.title: Resolve the conditional documentation updates now
findings.body: Three Documentation Updates bullets defer the decision to the implementer: `docs/testing/README.md` 'if that file's conventions require it', `AGENTS.md` 'unless the developer adds a `benchmark:sweep` script', and `docs/project/...` 'only if those docs enumerate every review mode; verify against their current content'. This is the 'update as needed' pattern REVIEW.md flags. Read the files at plan time and either list the required edit or declare it intentionally unnecessary.

findings.title: Align the AC1 assertions-checklist item with the plan's terminal-failure partition
findings.body: The checklist line for AC1 says 'terminal failures after the request record `not_determined` on the logs only', but the plan and runbook Step 6 partition on whether the finding result was established: a failure after parsing (for example in the publication path) keeps the ordinary `produced_findings`/`produced_none` values. As written the checklist would accept the publication-keyed behavior that the plan's Testing Strategy scenario 5 test exists to reject. Restate the checklist item to match Step 6 and `run-review-pass.ts` step 4.

findings.title: Define the AC14 exemption for committed campaign outputs
findings.body: Scenario 7 scans 'every committed evidence/fixture file ... under the benchmark tree and under `docs/testing/ronda/`' and fails on `sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `Bearer …` and similar shapes, while the same step requires committing the campaign outputs (`sweep-on-extended.json` etc.) whose finding bodies will quote the new credential-shaped seed that scenario 7 also requires. The only exemption stated is for seeds declared non-functional in the manifest; the evidence documents have none. Define how committed evidence that quotes declared non-functional fixture data is exempted, or the AC14 test will fail on the evidence the plan requires.

findings.title: Add the Plan Authoring Rigor per-rule outcome record
findings.body: The plan carries no per-rule outcome record for the six Plan Authoring Rigor rules (Sampling an external output distribution; One normative statement per fact; Counts of codebase artifacts; Independent verification of existence claims; Expectations at the composed call site; A conditional obligation names its scope) with a `Satisfied` / `Not applicable` / `Unsatisfied` outcome, its rationale and the revision it was evaluated at, and the empty PR description supplies none either. REVIEW.md's Plan authoring rigor backstop treats a missing outcome record (or evidence recorded only in PR comments) as blocking per Group H. This plan fires several of the rules hard and needs the record: Rule 3/Rule 4 on 'the three `ModelClient`-referencing test files are the complete set (`grep -rl ModelClient tests/`)', '`redactForbiddenValues` path already exists in the benchmark classifier', 'nothing currently surfaces the provider-reported model'; Rule 1 on the classifier's dependence on model-produced finding text naming an identifier or `matchTerm`; Rule 5 on the `ModelClient.complete` return-shape change with five consumers; Rule 6 on the conditional Documentation Updates steps. Add the outcome record with the evidence re-run at the recorded revision.

findings.title: PR description carries no Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so this plan PR has no `Document Quality Gate` log and no `Matrix coherence preflight` row. The plan contains a stateful contract — the 'Decision-gate matrix (plan-time classification)' section, the three-value per-category outcome (`produced_findings` / `produced_none` / `not_determined`) and the evidence-tier lifecycle in the `sweep-real-pr-evidence.md` bullet — so the preflight row may not read `Not applicable — no stateful contract`. Add a current log to the PR description containing the six-check matrix-coherence audit summary for these rows.

findings.title: Degraded-record boundary contradicts AC1/AC18/AC19
findings.body: `src/core/run-review-pass.ts` rules 1–2 hold both degraded records pending and emit nothing until `deps.model.complete` is called, on the argument that 'a pass that dies between the two — an authoritative-document fetch or any other GitHub error raised after `readChangedFiles` and before `deps.model.complete` — reached nothing and owes no sweep record at all, not even a degraded one'. AC1 does not place the boundary there: it names 'a GitHub error raised after the changed files are read but before that result is available' as a terminal failure **after** review execution whose logs carry the per-category record for the categories it reached, and AC18/AC19 attach the unrecognized-enablement and `sweep-did-not-run` records to a pass that 'reaches review execution', not to one that issues a review request; AC1's 'emits no ... sweep-did-not-run record' sentence is scoped to failures **before** review execution (a missing credential, a config load error, a deadline abort or GitHub error raised before the changed files are read). Testing Strategy scenario 5 and runbook Steps 4–5 then assert 'zero sweep metadata on every surface' for that window, locking the deviation into the test contract. Either cite spec text that limits the degraded records to an issued review request, or emit the degraded record on the logs for a failure after the changed-files read (with an empty reached set), and align the plan, scenario 5 and the runbook.

findings.title: `--runs 1` cannot keep today's output identical
findings.body: Implementation Order step 11 says of `--runs <n>`: 'Default 1 keeps today's single-run output identical.' The same step then states that 'Every run record of **both** arms also carries the `fixture` and `configuration` identity blocks ... they are part of the output shape, unconditional on the sweep', and the output-shape bullet adds the model-call count and elapsed time to every record (plus `sweepPerCategory`/`sweepListVersion` for sweep-on). A default `--runs 1` invocation therefore does not produce today's JSON, and the plan never defines the envelope for n>1 ('`--runs 2` yields two per-run records in one file' — array? wrapper object?). State the actual compatibility story (e.g. additive fields only, envelope shape for n>1) instead of the identical-output claim.

findings.title: Fixture seed file paths are left as 'or similar'
findings.body: Every row of the Seed Data table gives the seed's target path as '`src/benchmark/git-history.ts` or similar', '`src/benchmark/output.ts` or similar', '`src/benchmark/guard.ts` or similar', '`src/benchmark/records.ts` or similar', '`src/benchmark/credentials.ts` or similar'. The patches and the seeded-defect matching depend on the actual file paths and content, so the implementer must invent them; the plan does not establish whether `src/benchmark/` even exists. Pin each seed to a concrete, verified path and describe the planted defect precisely enough that the patch and its match metadata are determined, as the plan does for everything else.

findings.title: `matchTerms` is used with two different meanings
findings.body: The recorded sweep list carries `matchTerms` — 'a non-empty array of lowercase literal substrings drawn from the category's `failureShape` wording, which the deterministic classifier ... matches against finding text'. The Seed Data table uses the same name for the benchmark seed's own metadata ('matchTerms over "head", "api", "evidence"/"inference"'), while Implementation Order step 10 refers to the manifest's real key as `matchTermGroups` ('legacy `matchTermGroups` shape included'). Three names now cover two unrelated notions (category classification in `sweep-categories.json` versus finding-to-seed matching in `tests/fixtures/recall-benchmark/manifest.json`). Rename one of them and state which key each file actually carries.

findings.title: Validator adds a malformed condition AC19 does not define
findings.body: `src/review/sweep-categories.ts` is described as validating 'per AC19', but its rule set requires '`matchTerms` (non-empty array of non-blank strings)' as well. AC19's malformed definition is closed: it enumerates the AC4 fields (identifier, display label, description, failure shape, evidence source, positive-integer count), duplicate identifiers, zero categories, and the list version's domain — `matchTerms` is not among them. Under the plan, a list that satisfies every AC4 field but omits `matchTerms` is reported `sweep-did-not-run` with no list version, whereas AC19 defines such a list as well-formed. Either drop it from the validity domain or record it as a deliberate tightening beyond AC19 (and stop citing it, and Testing Strategy scenario 2's 'every malformed shape AC19 names ... missing/empty/non-string `matchTerms`', as AC19-derived).

findings.title: Documentation updates are left as unresolved conditionals
findings.body: `docs/testing/README.md` — 'index the new runbook and evidence artifacts if that file's conventions require it'; `docs/project/1-business-domain.md` and `docs/project/3-software-architecture.md` — 'add the sweep mode ... only if those docs enumerate every review mode; verify against their current content during implementation'. These are documentation decisions the plan leaves to the implementer to guess, exactly the 'update as needed' pattern REVIEW.md flags as important. Read the three files now and either schedule the concrete edit or declare it unnecessary with the reason.

findings.title: Campaign commands rely on unverified `--manifest`/`--patches` flags
findings.body: Runbook Step 8's original-thirteen control leg runs `npx tsx src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts --sweep-mode off --runs 5 --manifest tests/fixtures/recall-benchmark/original-thirteen/manifest.json --patches .../patches.json --output-file ...`. Implementation Order step 11 introduces only `--sweep-mode`, `--runs` and `--output-file` and says the parser is extended 'in the existing `parseArgs` style'; the Verification Log never establishes that `--manifest`/`--patches` exist or accept these values. If they do not, the whole original-fixture control — required by AC8's baseline comparability rule — cannot run. Verify the existing flag surface and record the check, or add the flags to the Implementation Order.

findings.title: Hardcoded source line numbers and existence claims are unverified
findings.body: The plan leans on source references and existence/count claims that cannot be confirmed from the document and are not marked 'unverified — implementer must confirm before proceeding': `src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts:447-449` (single controller/timer), `src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts:475-489` (shared-model `Promise.all`), `.github/workflows/ronda-review.yml` L134–145, `src/cli/review-pr.ts` L81–90, `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` L224–233, `tests/unit/webhook/webhook-job.test.ts` L111, `tests/unit/cli/recall-benchmark.test.ts` L26/L243, `tests/integration/review-pass.test.ts` L84/L223/L304, `tests/unit/webhook/webhook-server.test.ts` L1104/L1434/L1502/L1634, plus 'the three `ModelClient`-referencing test files are the complete set' and '`redactForbiddenValues` ... already exists'. These drive real decisions (per-request model identity, the `--runs` timer relocation, the test-double migration list). Re-run the checks and record the outputs in the Verification Log, or mark each claim unverified; hardcoded line numbers will also drift before implementation.

findings.title: Model-identity seam is untraced product scope
findings.body: `src/inference/model-client.ts` / `src/inference/openai-compatible-client.ts` are changed to make `ModelClient.complete` return `{ content, reportedModel? }`, touching five production call sites and three test-double families, so that AC8/AC9's 'immutable model version' can be recorded. The spec frames that value as a field of the committed *evidence* (Use Case 3 'Information shown', AC8), i.e. operator-recorded; no acceptance criterion schedules an interface return-shape change. The plan's own analysis concedes the reported string 'is not itself proof of immutability' and that admissibility still depends on an operator-recorded version-attestation basis — so the product change does not by itself satisfy AC8/AC9. Either trace this change to an acceptance criterion and justify the cross-cutting risk, or record it as an optional implementation aid and keep the evidence requirement operator-side.

findings.title: Attribution entries mix 'parsed' and 'published' findings
findings.body: `SweepPassRecord` is defined as carrying 'a per-finding attribution entry for every published finding', and `SweepFindingAttribution` as 'one entry per published finding', but `classifyFindings` is specified to emit 'one attribution entry per parsed finding' and Testing Strategy scenario 2 repeats 'one attribution entry per parsed finding in publication order'. The plan never states whether every parsed finding is published (or whether anything drops findings between parse and publication). AC20 is scoped to published findings, so the plan must say which set the record is keyed to and what happens to a parsed finding that is not published.

findings.title: 'outcome/attribution entry counts agreeing' is not testable as written
findings.body: Testing Strategy scenario 2 requires '**one attribution entry per parsed finding in publication order, with the outcome/attribution entry counts agreeing**'. Outcomes are one per category (five entries) and attributions are one per finding, so the two counts never 'agree' in any obvious sense, and the plan does not say what is being compared (e.g. the set of categories with `produced_findings` equals the set of distinct identifiers appearing in attribution entries). Replace it with a concrete, assertable invariant.

findings.title: Classifier depends on model free text with no sampled evidence
findings.body: Rule 1's concern applies here and is not discharged: attribution rests on the model naming 'that category's identifier in its own `title` or `body` text' (or coincidentally containing a `matchTerm`), which is externally produced free text. Every classifier test in scenario 2 and every benchmark assertion in scenario 6 use canned/fixture responses, so nothing establishes that real sweep-on runs actually name identifiers; if they never do, attribution silently collapses to `uncategorized` while AC20/AC9 still look satisfied. Add a campaign step that samples real sweep-on output, records the identifier-naming/attribution distribution (including the uncategorized rate), and fails closed if the primary signal never fires.

findings.title: Configuration-block equality assertion conflicts with unattested handling
findings.body: Implementation Order step 11's `configuration` block contains 'the **per-request provider-reported model identity** — every inference request's `reportedModel` captured from the response it came from', while the same step says 'where the endpoint reports none, or reports values that differ across the run set, or no attestation basis is recorded, the block states the version as unattested'. Testing Strategy scenario 6 nevertheless asserts '`configuration` blocks differing only in `sweepMode`'. When the endpoint reports nothing or reports varying values, the two arms can differ in more than `sweepMode` through no campaign asymmetry — and the plan elsewhere permits that as a recordable unattested state rather than a test failure. Separate fixed configuration from per-response observation (e.g. keep `reportedModel` out of the block compared for equality), or state explicitly which outcome wins.

findings.title: Summary misstates the record carried by the off path
findings.body: The Summary says 'every degraded path (off, unrecognized value, unreadable/empty/malformed list) degrades to the existing non-sweep review with the spec-mandated record and no failure'. The plan's own matrix row and AC18 give the recognized-off and absent cases *no* record; only the unrecognized and invalid-list cases carry one. Reword so the Summary does not imply an off run records a degradation.

findings.title: `ReviewPassResult.sweep` purpose does not match the benchmark path
findings.body: `src/domain/review-pass.types.ts` is specified to gain optional `ReviewPassResult.sweep` metadata 'for benchmark and caller surfaces', but the benchmark (`src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts`) never goes through a review pass: per the same section it returns its own `sweepPerCategory` / `sweepListVersion` record. Correct the stated purpose (pass callers only) or say how the two surfaces share the type.

findings.title: Recorded field is `findingInstanceCount` in one place, `count` in another
findings.body: The recorded-artifact bullet gives each category a `findingInstanceCount` from the spec's Statuses table, while `SweepCategory` in `src/domain/review-pass.types.ts` is listed with 'count' and the validator only says 'finding-instance count'. State the JSON key and the type field once and use the same name everywhere so the loader/validator field mapping is unambiguous.

findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log to the PR description
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required 'Document Quality Gate' log is missing. REVIEW.md requires every spec PR to carry a current log, and this spec contains a stateful contract — the evidence-tier table with its valid transitions (lines 520-539), the category-list currency rule (513-518) and the precision regression test (284-289) — so the log must also carry a 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary. Add the log with that row; a missing log is important by default, and a claim of unchecked coverage would make it blocking.

findings.title: Reconcile the initial category list with the ranking it claims to come from
findings.body: The 'Sweep categories (initial list)' table (490-496) and the Coverage Matrix O3 row (line 712: 'The five initial categories come from the 2026-09-23 sub-theme ranking') do not match the counts the spec itself reports. The list includes `guard-fails-open` at 5 finding instances while `Spec-AC-compliance` at 7 instances is left off the list (line 507), so an omitted theme outranks an included one. State the selection rule explicitly (for example 'top five product themes after excluding workflow-gate artifacts') with the counts that follow from it, or correct the O3 claim. As written, the AC4/AC6 evidence checks cannot tell whether the list is correctly scoped on real-PR evidence.

findings.title: The sweep has no satisfiable path while the list cannot be current
findings.body: Use Case 1's precondition requires 'A recorded sweep category list exists and is marked current' (line 38), AC1 requires consideration of 'every category on the current recorded list' (569-570), and the Business Rules require exactly one current list (420-422); but the Statuses section (513-518) and AC6 (583-590) say the recorded list 'cannot be marked current' while Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, and line 827 still asserts 'This spec is complete and documented.' Nothing in the document produces a current list, so the sweep, AC1, AC18, AC19 and AC20 cannot be satisfied. Define an interim current version (for example version 1 with the two undecided candidates recorded as explicitly deferred), or move list currency out of the Use Case 1 precondition, so the feature has a reachable delivery path.

findings.title: AC13 gives two non-equivalent definitions of 'harder'
findings.body: AC13 defines 'harder' behaviourally on line 618 ('not matched by the exact canonical form ... so that a guard recognizing only that canonical form would miss it') and then syntactically through four ways on 621-625, declaring those four ways exhaustive. A value 'wrapped in another construct' can still contain the canonical form verbatim and be matched by a substring guard, so it is harder under the four-way list but not under the behavioural test; conversely an added qualifier counts as harder under the list even if the guard is unanchored. Pick one test (the behavioural one, checked against the recorded canonical baseline form) and make the four ways illustrative, not exhaustive, so the criterion is checkable.

findings.title: Name the surface for the degraded-sweep records; AC3 currently forbids the obvious one
findings.body: Several requirements say the pass 'records' something without defining the surface: Use Case 1 (99-105), the Business Rule at 423-426, AC18 (665-667, 'records ... that the enablement value was unrecognized') and AC19 (line 673, 'records that the sweep did not run'). Operational Visibility defines only the review summary, the per-category pass record (sweep passes only) and permissive logs ('may record', line 560). If these records land in the review summary, AC3's 'a non-sweep pass says neither' (line 577) and AC18's 'no sweep statement in the summary' (669-670) are violated. Specify the surface for each degraded case and reconcile it with AC3.

findings.title: State that the recall and precision comparison depends on the extended fixture
findings.body: Use Case 3's preconditions (170-172) require only 'the seeded benchmark', but its own consideration (212-217) and AC8 (593-598) require results reported on the extended fixture, with the original thirteen seeds as a subset. An operator following Use Case 3 as written produces results on the 13-defect fixture that AC8 rejects. Add the Use Case 5 fixture extension (AC12/AC13) as an explicit precondition or ordering constraint for Use Cases 3 and 4, and say whether any recall/precision evidence recorded before the extension must be re-run or is invalid.

findings.title: Reconcile AC15(a) with the matched-control requirement and define 'effect claim'
findings.body: AC15(a) makes the tier the boundary for a 'real-pull-request effect claim' ('no real-pull-request effect claim appears under a tier below Real-PR evidence (measured)'), which implies such a claim is permitted once the tier is measured. The Business Rules (454-461), Use Case 6's Considerations (399-409) and the evidence-tier table (line 526) instead require a matched sweep-off control for any comparative claim, and that control may never exist (Open Question 9). AC15(a) should carry the matched-control condition, and 'real-pull-request effect claim' needs a definition that distinguishes a descriptive miss record (permitted at provisional/measured) from a comparative effect claim, since the enum already permits labelled 'indicative' findings at the provisional tier.

findings.title: AC18 over-prescribes the configuration mechanism
findings.body: AC18 specifies the resolution chain — 'environment or workflow input over the operator config file over the built-in default, the same surface that already carries the durability-mode switch' (659-663) — which is implementation design, not product behaviour. The product requirement is that an operator can enable or disable the sweep per repository, that an absent value means off, and that an unrecognized value is off and recorded. Move the precedence chain and the durability-mode-switch reference to the implementation plan and keep AC18 to the observable behaviour.

findings.title: Display labels are not shown in review summaries
findings.body: Line 486 says display labels are what operators read 'in the recorded list and in review summaries', but AC3 (576-577) and Operational Visibility (545-548) put only sweep activation and the list version in the summary, and the per-category breakdown is deliberately kept out of the review body (549-554; Out of Scope 745-746). Drop 'and in review summaries', or state which labels, if any, appear there.

findings.title: Define the category list version identifier format
findings.body: AC7 requires the list to 'carry a version' and AC3 requires the review summary to state 'which category list version was used', but no identifier format (date, integer, hash) is defined anywhere. AC15(c)'s relabeling and the pull-request count restart also key off list-version identity, and the Business Rule counts reviews 'under the current category list version'. Define the format so AC3/AC7 can be checked and operators can tell whether two reviews used the same list.

findings.title: Pin down how many harder credential-pattern cases are required
findings.body: Use Case 5's postcondition says the fixture contains 'credential-pattern cases' (plural, line 323) and the Business Rules require 'harder credential-pattern variants' (451-453), while AC13 requires only 'at least one' (line 615). State the required count in AC13 or use the singular consistently so the criterion is unambiguous.

findings.title: Add explicit triggers to the use cases
findings.body: Use Cases 2-6 have no Trigger, and Use Case 1's trigger exists only as a precondition line ('through any of its normal review triggers', line 40). The template expects actor, trigger, steps, outcome. One line per use case (for example 'triggered when the operator runs the benchmark', 'triggered when new evidence arrives') removes ambiguity about when each flow starts and who initiates it.

findings.title: Add the required Document Quality Gate log to the PR description
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required `Document Quality Gate` log is absent. REVIEW.md requires spec PRs to include a current log; a missing log is an important finding by default. Add the log — including the `Matrix coherence preflight` row (see the separate matrix finding) — before requesting review.

findings.title: Add a decision-gate consistency matrix for the sweep enablement and evidence-tier gates
findings.body: The spec adds stateful decision-gate behavior — AC18 (enablement: absent/empty/unrecognized → off; recognized on/off → sweep) and the evidence-tier state machine in `Statuses / Enum Values` — but the only matrix present is the `Coverage Matrix` (objective → AC). REVIEW.md requires a consistency matrix or pointer identifying gate inputs, allowed outcomes, required next actions, mirror surfaces, and examples for complex gate behavior; missing matrix evidence is blocking before `ready-for-human-review`. Add the matrix (or a pointer) and the corresponding `Matrix coherence preflight` row to the Quality Gate log.

findings.title: Resolve the contradiction between 'exactly one list is current' and 'the list cannot be marked current'
findings.body: Business Rule (line 420) says 'Exactly one sweep category list is current at any time,' and the evidence tiers, the review-summary version (AC3), the UC1 precondition (line 38), and UC2 `Information shown` (line 139, 'the date it became current') all depend on a current list. But `Statuses / Enum Values` (line 516) and AC6 (lines 583–590) state that while Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved 'the recorded list cannot be marked current.' That makes the Business Rule unsatisfiable and leaves every currency-dependent requirement without a valid list. Either resolve OQ1/OQ8 in this spec or make the currency rule conditional and define what the sweep, tier, and version surfaces do before a list is current.

findings.title: Reconcile the 'tied fifth' ranking with guard-fails-open (5 instances) being swept
findings.body: `Candidates awaiting a human decision` (line 507) says spec-AC-compliance has 7 instances and is 'tied fifth in the sub-theme ranking,' while the swept list includes `guard-fails-open` with only 5 instances (line 496) and `record-identity` with 7. A 7-instance theme cannot rank fifth below a 5-instance theme. State the ranking basis (and whether excluded/undecided themes are counted) and fix either the 'tied fifth' label or the initial five-category list; as written, O3's claim that the five categories come from the ranking is not verifiable.

findings.title: Reconcile the category instance counts with the cited 79 real findings
findings.body: The initial list totals 43 instances (14+9+8+7+5), the excluded list adds 10, and the undecided candidates add 7+4 — 64 in total — while Deferral Note D1 quotes 'the 79 real findings' (line 727). The spec never accounts for the remaining 15 findings or states the ranking cutoff. Because O2/O3 and AC6 justify the list by real-PR evidence, state the residual/uncategorized count or the cutoff rule; otherwise the evidence basis for the list is incomplete.

findings.title: Add the extended-fixture dependency to Use Case 3's preconditions
findings.body: UC3's preconditions (lines 170–172) require only that 'the seeded benchmark … is available' and that both configurations can run, but UC3's Considerations (lines 212–217) mandate that the comparison be 'reported on the extended fixture' produced by UC5. As written, an operator can satisfy UC3's preconditions with the 2026-09-10 fixture and produce results the same section calls inadmissible. Add 'UC5 complete / extended fixture version available' as a precondition (and to UC4, which inherits UC3's runs).

findings.title: Reconcile the matched sweep-off control with the one-review-per-head-SHA contract
findings.body: UC6 (lines 405–406) says a comparative claim 'requires a matched control: a sweep-off review of the same pull request heads, with the same model and configuration, recorded but not published.' UC1 (lines 73–75) says 'A head that already has its one review is not reviewed a second time because the sweep was toggled,' and the Business Rules/AC2 (lines 417–419, 573–575) keep 'one review per head SHA.' Re-running a sweep-off pass on the same head is a second review of that head. Define how the control runs without violating the one-review contract (including whether an unpublished pass counts as a review), or scope the control differently.

findings.title: Clarify whether 'no sweep-enabled review recorded' is version-scoped after a list revision
findings.body: AC15(b) (lines 641–642) labels evidence `fixture_only` when 'no sweep-enabled real pull request review recorded,' while AC15(c) (lines 647–651) and the transitions (lines 535–539) say a revision restarts the count at zero but leaves the tier at `real_pr_provisional`. If 'recorded' is read against the current list version, a post-revision record with zero counted PRs satisfies both `fixture_only` (zero) and `real_pr_provisional` ('fewer than ten … accumulated,' line 525). State that the labels are version-scoped or reword AC15(b) so the post-revision tier is unambiguous.

findings.title: Define 'external-finding evidence' and 'adjudicated'
findings.body: The measured-tier gate (Business Rule line 456, AC15(b) line 638, and the `real_pr_measured` definition) turns on whether 'their external-finding evidence has been adjudicated,' but neither term is defined anywhere in the spec. Without a definition of what counts as external-finding evidence, who adjudicates it, and what 'adjudicated' means, AC15(b) cannot be tested and the gate can be satisfied or failed by interpretation.

findings.title: Enumerate the recognized on/off values for the enablement setting
findings.body: AC18 (lines 663–666) says the sweep is off when the value is 'empty or is not a recognized on or off value,' but never lists the recognized values (for example `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`, `1`/`0`, `enabled`/`disabled`). The unrecognized-value behavior — publish normally and record that the value was unrecognized — is untestable until the accepted set is defined. The key name may be deferred to planning; the value grammar may not.

findings.title: Resolve AC14's ban on credential values with AC13's requirement to plant one
findings.body: AC13 (line 618) requires each harder fixture case to plant a 'sensitive name or value,' and UC5 (lines 314–315) adds credential-pattern variants; but AC14 (lines 630–631) and the Business Rule (lines 477–478) say quality evidence 'contains no credential values, tokens, or authorization values.' UC5 permits synthetic values ('must not contain real credential values,' line 344), but AC14 omits the 'real' qualifier. As written, the fixture AC13 requires violates AC14. Clarify that only real secrets are forbidden and synthetic pattern strings are allowed.

findings.title: Use one definition of 'harder' in AC13
findings.body: AC13 gives two definitions (lines 617–625): behavioral ('not matched by the exact canonical form … so that a guard recognizing only that canonical form would miss it') and structural ('differs from the canonical form in at least one of these ways'). These can disagree — a case that differs only in letter case still matches a case-insensitive canonical guard, and a case that differs in none of the four ways but is missed by the canonical match is 'harder' under the first sentence and not under the second. Make the structural rule operative (or state their equivalence) so the fixture check is deterministic.

findings.title: Disambiguate 'real-pull-request effect claim'
findings.body: 'Real-pull-request effect' is used for two different things: AC15(a) (line 634) forbids an 'effect claim' below `real_pr_measured`, while the tier table (line 526) says `real_pr_measured` permits 'descriptive real-pull-request claims' and reserves 'comparative effect claims' for a matched control; the Business Rule (line 454) says 'effect … may not be claimed until ten' but then allows 'only a descriptive … record.' Define 'effect claim' (descriptive vs. comparative) or replace it with the two specific terms so AC15(a) can be checked.

findings.title: Make the regression-gate restoration trigger consistent
findings.body: AC17 (lines 654–656) says the gate is 'restored once [the AC12 and AC13 cases] exist' — existence alone restores it — while UC5 Step 4 (line 318) requires that 'the operator declares the extended fixture usable as a regression gate.' State whether restoration is automatic on existence or requires a recorded human declaration; as written the gate can be both restored and not restored at the same moment.

findings.title: Define what a 'clean result' review publishes
findings.body: AC10 (lines 607–608) requires a pass that finds nothing to 'publish a clean result,' but the spec never says what that review contains — an empty review, a 'no issues found' comment, or no review at all — while elsewhere it insists on one review per head SHA. Define the clean-result output so AC10 is testable.

findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log (including a Matrix coherence preflight row)
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so there is no `Document Quality Gate` log. The checklist requires a current log in the PR description; a missing log is an important finding by default. This spec also contains a stateful contract — the Evidence tier table with four valid transitions, the enablement/degradation decision rules in Use Case 1, AC18 and AC19, and the per-category pass record — so once the log exists, its `Matrix coherence preflight` row must carry the six-check audit summary for that state table rather than `Not applicable — no stateful contract`. Add the log with that row.

findings.title: A compliant category list can never be current, so the sweep can never run
findings.body: `Statuses / Enum Values` says "Exactly one recorded category list version is current. Every candidate is either swept ... or explicitly excluded with a recorded rationale" and then, two lines later, "While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, the recorded list ... cannot be marked current" (repeated in AC6). Use Case 1's first precondition is "A recorded sweep category list exists and is marked current", and AC1/AC2/AC3/AC20 all assume a pass against the current list. As written, no list can satisfy its own currency rule, so the feature cannot run and AC4/AC6 leave it permanently unimplementable. Separately, if a list exists but is not marked current, the degradation rules (Use Case 1's last consideration, the Business Rules, AC19) cover only "cannot be read, empty, or malformed" — not "present but not current" — so that pass's behavior is undefined. Either allow a current list that records OQ1/OQ8 candidates as explicitly pending, or add "list present but not marked current" to the degradation set and say what the pass does.

findings.title: AC15 gives three different labels for the zero-count case
findings.body: AC15(b) says "a record with nine or fewer counted pull requests ... is labeled Real-PR evidence (provisional)" — which includes zero — and in the same sentence says "one with no sweep-enabled real pull request review recorded is labeled Fixture evidence only". AC15(c) adds a third outcome: after a list revision the label is Relabeled Real-PR evidence (provisional) while "the counted pull requests restart at zero", so a record with zero counted reviews is provisional there and Fixture-only under AC15(b). The Evidence tier table's provisional description ("Fewer than ten pull requests ... have accumulated") and the transition "Fixture evidence only → Real-PR evidence (provisional) when the first ... is recorded" do not settle it either. Make the zero-count rule single-valued and align AC15(b), AC15(c), the enum descriptions, and the transition list.

findings.title: "Configuration" must be identical across the compared runs but contains the sweep flag
findings.body: Use Case 3 requires "Model and configuration must be identical across the compared runs; otherwise the comparison measures something else", and Use Case 4 and the Business Rules require the "same target, model, configuration, and fixture version" for sweep-off and sweep-on runs. But AC18 makes the sweep enablement part of "the effective operator configuration value for the run". Read literally, the only comparison this feature permits is between two configurations that differ, which its own admissibility rule forbids — so every recall, variance, precision, and cost comparison is inadmissible by construction. The matched control has the same problem ("same model and configuration" while sweep-off). Define "configuration" once as everything held fixed excluding sweep enablement, and use that wording in Use Case 3, Use Case 4, and the Business Rules.

findings.title: The ten-pull-request count is defined three incompatible ways
findings.body: Use Case 6 step 1 counts "the pull requests that carried a Ronda review under the current category list version", as does this Business Rule; AC15(b) requires those pull requests to have "been sweep-enabled and reviewed"; and Use Case 6's consideration says "The count in this gate counts sweep-enabled reviews only." Because the sweep ships off by default and is enabled per repository (AC18, and the Business Rule "This feature ships the sweep off unless a repository enables it"), a pull request reviewed with the sweep disabled would count under Use Case 6 and this rule but not under AC15. Also unstated: whether the unit is pull requests or reviewed head SHAs (Ronda reviews per head SHA), and whether a pass that degraded to non-sweep because the list was unreadable counts toward the ten. Define the counting unit once and use the same words in AC15, Use Case 6, and the Business Rules.

findings.title: The matched sweep-off control is undefined and collides with one-review-per-head
findings.body: Use Case 6's consideration requires, for a comparative claim, "a sweep-off review of the same pull request heads, with the same model and configuration, recorded but not published". That conflicts with the Business Rule "One review per head SHA, containing every finding from the pass, still holds with the sweep active": the spec never says how a second, unpublished pass for an already-reviewed head is run, whether it counts as that head's one review, or whether the existing one-review-per-head and supersede enforcement would skip it entirely. It also asks for the same review contract without a publication route that the contract defines. Either define the unpublished control pass as an explicitly separate mode that cannot publish and cannot consume the head's single review, or delete the matched-control mechanism and leave Open Question 9 framed without it.

findings.title: AC18 and AC19 require records with no defined surface, and conflict with AC3
findings.body: AC18 requires the pass to record "without exposing the raw value, that the enablement value was unrecognized", and AC19 requires it to record "that the sweep did not run", but no surface is defined for either. `Operational Visibility` only says logs "may record that the sweep ran" (permissive, not a requirement), and AC18 itself rules out the summary ("no sweep statement in the summary") and the per-category pass record ("no per-category pass record") for a disabled sweep. As written the requirement cannot be verified; if the intended surface is the review summary it contradicts AC3's "a non-sweep pass says neither". Name the surface, and use the same one for AC18 and AC19.

findings.title: AC18 never lists which values count as "a recognized on or off value"
findings.body: AC18 turns the sweep on for "a recognized on or off value" and off for "an empty or ... not a recognized on or off value", but the recognized vocabulary is never enumerated (on/off? true/false? 1/0? enabled/disabled?). The key name is explicitly deferred as "a planning decision", which is acceptable, but the accepted value set is not — so implementers must guess the contract and the unrecognized-value branch is untestable. Enumerate the accepted on and off values explicitly and state that everything else is off and recorded as unrecognized.

findings.title: The initial list has no stated selection rule, so completeness cannot be checked
findings.body: This section claims the list accounts for every candidate, but the named counts are 43 swept (14+9+8+7+5) + 10 planted-proof + 7 spec-AC-compliance + 4 per-finding resolution = 64 finding instances, while the corpus is described as 79 real findings (Deferral Note D1). No cutoff or selection rule is stated, so a reader cannot tell why the list stops after five categories, why the four-instance per-finding-resolution theme is still a candidate, and what happened to the remaining themes that account for the other ~15 instances. AC6 only requires "every candidate category considered", which is trivially satisfiable. State the selection rule (for example an instance-count cutoff, and how the tied-fifth-place theme was handled) and either account for the remaining themes or say they are below the cutoff.

findings.title: AC13's 'exhaustive' four ways do not match the category table's five variants
findings.body: AC13 declares four exhaustive ways, merging "a qualifier or prefix added to the name", while the `credential-pattern-gap` description in `Statuses / Enum Values` lists "qualified, camelCase, hyphenated, prefixed, or wrapped" as five distinct variants. Use one vocabulary in both places and say whether "qualified" and "prefixed" are one way or two, so the fixture author and the checker apply the same rule.

findings.title: AC10 leaves "clean result" undefined
findings.body: AC10 requires a pass that finds nothing to "publish a clean result", but "clean result" is defined nowhere: is it a review with no findings, a review-body statement, a check-run conclusion, or nothing published at all? Given the review contract is comment-only and this spec elsewhere avoids publishing empty category lists, state exactly what is published and where so the criterion is verifiable.

findings.title: Unify the real-PR recall denominator with AC15(d)'s sweep-claim membership rule
findings.body: AC15(d) defines the recall denominator as the confirmed defects *within the sweep's claim*, decided against the recorded category list, and explicitly excludes defects that fit no swept category ("a finding that fits none of the swept categories is recorded uncategorized (AC20) and lies outside the claim, so it is not a confirmed defect for this measurement"). The Business Rules section's real-PR bullet states the same denominator without that filter — "a defect counts when a compared reviewer reported it, Ronda's sweep-enabled review, Ronda's sweep-off control, or the external reviewer alike" — excluding only `ronda_better` and the Ronda-finding-rejected outcome, and Coverage Matrix O11 does the same. Both are declared mirror surfaces of the claim-admissibility gate. Consequence: an external-reviewer (or control) finding that matches no swept category is in the denominator under the Business Rules/O11 reading and out of it under AC15(d), so the same cohort yields two different recall figures and two different numerator sets. Pick AC15(d) as the only normative definition and make the Business Rules bullet and O11 reference it instead of restating the metric.

findings.title: Define finding-level entries in the per-category pass record
findings.body: AC1 and Use Case 1 define the record only at category granularity: the check-run output and logs "each show, per category, whether that category produced findings or none", and Use Case 1's Information shown says the same. But AC20 requires *every published finding* to "appear in the per-category pass record ... either against one or more swept categories or as uncategorized", AC9 requires attributing "each sweep-on unexpected finding to the category (or categories, or uncategorized) recorded for it", and AC15(d) derives sweep-claim membership from "its per-category pass record entry". No finding-level entry, field set, or representation for a finding that fits several categories is ever specified, so AC20 cannot be verified as written and implementers must invent the record's shape. Add the finding-level structure to AC1 (which the matrix declares the sole owner of the surface rule) or weaken AC20/AC9/AC15(d) to what a category-level record can support.

findings.title: Add the missing Document Quality Gate log and Matrix coherence preflight row
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required current `Document Quality Gate` log is missing; REVIEW.md makes a missing log an important finding by default. Additionally, this spec contains stateful contracts (the Decision-gate consistency matrix, the evidence-tier state table and transitions, and the enablement/list precedence rules), so the log must carry a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary rather than a not-applicable claim. Add the log, including that row, before requesting human review.

findings.title: Qualify AC6 to the initial list version
findings.body: AC6 requires that "The swept list holds exactly the five categories in Statuses / Enum Values", with the excluded entries fixed to the four never-found kinds, planted-proof evidence, spec-AC-compliance, and per-finding resolution. Use Case 2 and AC7 define a revision model that adds, removes, and reorders categories under a new version with recorded evidence and date, and the tier rules anticipate revisions ("Revising the list restarts that count"). Any approved revision therefore makes AC6 false. Scope AC6 to the initial list version (or to the version delivered by this item) and let later versions be governed by AC7/Use Case 2.

findings.title: Use one definition of "harder" in AC13
findings.body: AC13 first defines a harder credential case as one whose planted sensitive name or value "is not matched by the exact canonical form the existing case uses", then states that the four ways (prefix/qualifier, different case convention, different separator, wrapping) "are the exhaustive set that AC13 counts; a variant that differs in none of them is not harder for AC13 purposes, however unusual it looks". A variant that differs in a fifth way — for example a synonym credential name, or a suffix that is not a qualifier — is harder under the first sentence and not harder under the second. State a single test (the four-way rule, with the canonical-form sentence as background) and make the fixture-record requirement check against that test.

findings.title: Resolve the review-body/check-run visibility conflict for the per-category record
findings.body: Operational Visibility says the per-category record "is never published in the review body, so reviewers of the pull request do not read a list of empty categories", but AC1 assigns the same record to the pass's check-run output, which is visible on the pull request too. As written, the stated purpose (keeping empty-category lists away from pull-request readers) is not achieved by the chosen surface. Decide whether the record is meant to be visible to pull-request readers (and fix the rationale) or whether it must not appear on the check-run output, and update AC1, the Pass-outcome surface row, and Operational Visibility together.

findings.title: Correct the enablement gate's mirror-surface citations
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix's "Sweep enablement resolution (AC18)" row names as mirror surfaces: "Business rule 'Whether the sweep is enabled is read from the effective operator configuration value' (~106); AC18; Use Case 1 step 1". No such rule exists in the Business Rules section; that sentence is in Use Case 1 → Considerations, and Use Case 1 step 1 ("Ronda starts a review pass for the pull request head") says nothing about enablement resolution. The row therefore requires agreement from sites that do not state the rule, while omitting the actual prose site. Point the mirror surfaces at AC18 and Use Case 1 Considerations so the gate's prose and table can actually be checked against each other.

findings.title: Define the sweep-did-not-run and unrecognized-enablement records in the enum section
findings.body: The Category list readability gate row uses `sweep-did-not-run` as a normative code value ("the pass records `sweep-did-not-run`, reporting no list version as used"), but Statuses / Enum Values never lists that record type (no display label, no allowed domain), and the unrecognized-enablement record required by AC18 has no code value at all. Operational Visibility then merges the two under one name — "A sweep-did-not-run record ... states that the sweep did not run because its category list was unreadable, empty, or malformed (AC19), or that a non-empty enablement value was unrecognized (AC18)" — while the decision matrix treats them as distinct records. Add both record types to the enum section with labels and keep them distinct at every site.

findings.title: Make AC8's baseline-comparability requirement unambiguous
findings.body: AC8 says "Baseline comparability requires a repeated original-fixture comparison" (both arms, at least the baseline's sample count) but then introduces a different concept: "Baseline reproduction is required only where the baseline document records a prompt revision, the inference parameters, and an immutable model version", concluding that because the 2026-09-10 baseline records only a command, a sample count, and a mutable alias, "no run against it is classified as baseline reproduction". Use Case 3, the Business Rules, and O5 then require "the recorded baseline-comparison configuration AC8 defines", a term AC8 never uses. A reader cannot tell whether the repeated two-arm original-fixture run is mandatory or dissolved by the reproduction caveat, nor which configuration it must record. Replace the reproduction paragraph with one rule (run both arms at least N times on the original fixture, record the model identity and effective review configuration the runs used, claim no comparison against the recorded alias) and use that same name everywhere.

findings.title: Add defect identity and matched category to the terminal miss record
findings.body: The Terminal miss record section defines a "head-level adjudication record ... carrying one entry for each reviewer whose miss it records, with these code values" `sweep_enabled_miss` and `external_review_miss`. But AC15(d) and the claim-admissibility gate require the membership decision for "a defect only human adjudication records" to be "recorded with the cohort's evidence before the claim is read" and recorded "by that adjudication naming the swept category the defect matches", and the denominator counts such a defect. The record has no field for the defect's identity or location and no field for the matched swept category, and it does not say how two such defects on one head are represented. Add the defect identity and matched-category fields (and the multiplicity rule) to the record, or name the record that carries them.

findings.title: State when and by whom the eligible-cohort cutoff is recorded
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) require the eligible cohort to be closed by "a recorded cutoff fixed in advance, before any eligible pass's findings are visible", and every member to be terminally adjudicated before the count is read. Nothing states who records the cutoff or when. Strictly read, a compliant cutoff must be recorded before the first eligible pass completes (its review is published, so its findings are visible), yet the spec starts from an already-running dogfooding deployment ("Ronda already reviews this repository's own pull requests"). Define the recording point (e.g. at sweep enablement, before the first eligible pass completes) and what an operator does if the sweep is already producing reviews, so the anti-cherry-picking rule is satisfiable rather than retroactively violated.

findings.title: Disambiguate "clean result"
findings.body: "Clean result" carries two meanings: the adjudication outcome `clean_agreement` in the tier and counting rules ("once that clean result is confirmed by the recorded same-head external review"), and a review with no findings in AC10 ("publishes a clean result"). Use distinct wording in AC10 (for example "a review with no findings") so the two cannot be read as the same state.

findings.title: Add explicit triggers to the use cases
findings.body: The repository's use-case template asks for actor, trigger, steps, and outcome; none of these use cases has a Trigger field, and for Use Case 6 it matters most: nothing says what event starts the cohort closure and adjudication (a schedule, the tenth eligible review, a manual decision). Add a Trigger line per use case, especially where the trigger interacts with the cutoff rule.

findings.title: Define "a check run whose outcome is a review"
findings.body: AC1 and the Pass-outcome surface assignment row pivot on "a check run whose outcome is a review", a condition GitHub does not define (check runs have conclusions, not review outcomes). The examples imply the existing success check run that carries the review, but the term is load-bearing for every surface assignment and should be defined once, concretely, in AC1.

findings.title: Keep AC1 to product-visible surfaces, not existing-flow mechanics
findings.body: AC1 restates existing internal failure-path mechanics — "a failure persisting the check-run recovery state", "a success check-run write that fails after its bounded retry", "the pass synthesizes no failure check run", "the failure surfaces through a non-zero process exit". Those are architecture-document facts; restating them in an acceptance criterion invites drift if that flow changes and makes the criterion much harder to verify. Reference the existing flow's rule and keep only the surface assignment AC1 owns.

findings.title: Define the counting unit for the ten-pull-request minimum

findings.title: Reconcile the provisional tier with the descriptive-claim gate

findings.title: Disambiguate AC10's 'clean result'
findings.body: AC10 requires a pass that finds nothing to 'publish a clean result', but 'clean result' already has a defined adjudication meaning in this spec (a head whose compared reviewers reported no findings, confirmed by the external review as `clean_agreement`). findings.title: Make AC10's anti-manufacture clause testable
findings.body: 'A review pass that finds nothing for every swept category and has no uncategorized finding ... produces no manufactured finding for any category' restates its own premise, so it cannot fail and does not test the risk the Considerations warn about (a list of categories inviting one finding each). Replace it with a falsifiable check — for example, a clean precision fixture run with the sweep on must publish the same empty result as its sweep-off run (AC9), and no finding may be attributed to a category the changed content cannot support — or drop the clause and rely on AC9's strict precision test.

findings.title: State how a sweep-off control pass runs and that it never publishes
findings.body: Use Case 6 requires a matched control 'recorded but not published' on heads that already carry their one review, but AC15(d) and the real-pull-request business rule only say the control 'is recorded with it'; no AC or business rule says the control pass must not publish or how it is executed. With AC2's one-review-per-head-SHA rule unchanged, and AC1/AC19 stating that an automatic run which finds the head's existing check run is skipped, a control run for an already-reviewed head would either be skipped or supersede the published review. Name the control's execution path (an offline run that publishes nothing, as benchmark runs do) and put the no-publication requirement where the claim gate can enforce it.

findings.title: Remove the duplicated trailing fragment in the Decision-gate consistency matrix

findings.title: Remove the duplicated 'used.' fragment in AC9

findings.title: AC2 does not define the existing-check automatic skip it is cited for

findings.title: 'Only site' claim for adjudication code values is contradicted by AC15(d)

findings.title: Terminal miss record leaves adjudicated defects without a terminal record
findings.body: The `Terminal miss record` section defines `sweep_enabled_miss`/`external_review_miss` only for a head "whose compared reviewers all reported no findings" and only for "a defect within the sweep's claim". AC15(b) makes a head not clean whenever "human adjudication recorded [a] defect", with no within-claim qualifier, and AC15(d) admits adjudication-recorded defects on heads that also carry findings. So an all-clean head whose adjudication records a defect outside the swept categories is neither a clean result nor entitled to a terminal miss record, and a mixed head's adjudication-only defect has no record type at all. In both cases the head cannot be terminally adjudicated, so the closed cohort cannot close and the ten-count is unreachable. Either scope the record to any adjudication-recorded defect (with an out-of-claim code value) or state that out-of-claim defects do not disturb a head's clean result.

findings.title: Make the eligible-cohort cutoff timing satisfiable and state when it is recorded
findings.body: Use Case 6 step 1, AC15(b) and the real-pull-request business rule all require the cutoff to be "fixed in advance, before any eligible pass's findings are visible". Once a sweep-enabled pass has published, any cutoff that admits it violates that condition, and a cutoff that excludes every published pass counts nothing, so the only satisfiable reading is that the cutoff is recorded before the sweep is enabled (or before the first candidate pass). The spec never says that: Use Case 6 presents cohort closure as part of the counting step, and its precondition assumes real-pull-request reviews have already accumulated. State the recording point explicitly and that no candidate pass may complete before it.

findings.title: AC13 defines "harder" twice in incompatible ways
findings.body: AC13 first says a case "is harder than baseline when the sensitive name or value it plants is not matched by the exact canonical form the existing case uses", then says "A case is harder when it differs ... in at least one of these ways" and "These four ways are the exhaustive set that AC13 counts; a variant that differs in none of them is not harder for AC13 purposes". A variant that differs from the canonical form in some fifth way satisfies the first sentence and fails the second, so the criterion is not decidable as written. Make the four-way list the sole test (or state that canonical-form non-match is necessary but not sufficient).

findings.title: Matrix mirror-surface pointers do not resolve to the sites they name

Name the exact section and bullet that restates each gate, or say the row is the sole owner.

findings.title: Decide whether real-PR evidence may be reported before ten counted pull requests
findings.body: Three sites disagree. The `Claim admissibility` row says "Descriptive real-pull-request claim: permitted at `real_pr_measured` alone", the `real_pr_provisional` tier says "Findings are indicative only, support no effect claim, and are labeled as such" (which presupposes reporting them), and Use Case 6's postcondition says "Real-pull-request evidence is read only as a descriptive record ..." with no threshold, while AC15(a) forbids only "effect claim[s]" below measured. As written an operator cannot tell whether the indicative sweep-enabled findings may be shown below ten. Fix one rule and align the tier row, the matrix row and AC15(a).

findings.title: Remove the leftover "used." in AC9
findings.body: AC9 reads "It records the category-list version and the effective review configuration the runs used." and then has a stray "used." on the following line before "It reports unexpected findings per configuration". findings.title: Remove the dangling fragment in the Claim admissibility example cell
findings.body: The `Claim admissibility` row's Example cell ends with the fragment "they do not pair the claim." after the sentence about a rerun control, repeating the sentence three clauses earlier. findings.title: Operational Visibility conflates the unrecognized-enablement record with sweep-did-not-run
findings.body: The `Per-category pass record` bullet describes a single "sweep-did-not-run record" that states either a list problem (AC19) or "that a non-empty enablement value was unrecognized (AC18)", while the decision matrix makes these two separate records with different rules. findings.title: "Clean result" is used with two different meanings
findings.body: AC10 uses "clean result" for a single pass's findings-free published review ("publishes a clean result"), while AC15(b) and Use Case 6 use it for a head whose compared reviewers were all clean and whose `clean_agreement` is confirmed. The ten-count depends on the second meaning and AC10 on the first. Use distinct names (for example "clean review" versus "clean head") so the adjudication rules cannot be read against the wrong object.
