findings.title: Cohort-closure rule deadlocks against the no-external-review rule
findings.body: The real-pull-request business rule closes the eligible cohort as every pull request that carried a sweep-enabled review up to a cutoff and requires that "every pull request in it must reach a terminal adjudication before the ten are counted" (lines 670-674; also Use Case 6 step 1, AC15(b), and the provisional→measured transition, which says an unadjudicated eligible pull request "blocks the transition"), while the same rules state here that "a pull request with no external review recorded is not adjudicated whether or not it carried findings". One eligible head with no recorded external review therefore makes the count unreadable forever and `real_pr_measured` unreachable — and the only escape, picking an earlier cutoff, reinstates exactly the favorable-case selection the rule exists to prevent, since nothing constrains how the cutoff is chosen. Define how such a pull request leaves the cohort (an explicit, recorded exclusion) or how it can be terminally adjudicated, and mirror the resolution in Use Case 6, AC15(b), the Evidence tier transitions, and the consistency matrix.

findings.title: AC1 contradicts itself on the check-run surface for a publishing pass
findings.body: AC1 states here that "For a pass that completes review execution and publishes a review, that write is a check run whose outcome is a review, so the record is on both surfaces", but later in the same criterion (lines 1030-1035) it says that for a pass whose review is already public the check run may be "the success outcome the pass reached, or none at all where the write never landed", with the record then on the logs only. The consistency matrix row "Pass-outcome surface assignment" follows the second reading ("A success check-run write that fails after its bounded retry leaves the record on the logs"). A publishing pass can therefore have no review-outcome check run, so the two sentences assign different surfaces to the same case. State one rule: the check-run copy exists only where the pass's own write produced a check run whose outcome is a review; otherwise the record is on the logs plus whatever surface that write produced.

findings.title: "Reached" makes partial per-category records impossible, contradicting Use Case 1
findings.body: AC1 defines reached so that it is binary — "the categories reached are exactly those the pass's request carried before the failure: a pass that fails before issuing any review request has reached none, and a pass that issued its request and then failed has reached every category its request carried" — yet Use Case 1 step 2 says a terminal-failure pass "records the categories it reached and no more" (line 52) and the Use Case 1 postcondition says "Every sweep pass that reaches review execution records, per category, ..." (line 76). A pass that reaches review execution but fails before issuing its request records nothing per category, contradicting that postcondition, and "and no more"/"each category it reached" describe a proper subset that AC1 says cannot exist. Either permit partial reach (record the categories actually considered) or state the all-or-nothing rule in Use Case 1 and fix the postcondition.

findings.title: Define the unpublished sweep-off control; it conflicts with one-review-per-head-SHA
findings.body: Every comparative real-PR claim requires "a sweep-off review of the same pull request heads, with the same model and configuration apart from the sweep setting, recorded but not published", and the tier transitions rely on "a control recorded on a head whose adjudication it reopens". Nothing defines how Ronda produces and stores a review that is never published: AC2 says that whenever the existing flow reaches publication "Ronda publishes exactly one review per head SHA" and that "The sweep adds no second publication path", and the business rule repeats "One review per head SHA ... still holds with the sweep active". Who triggers the control, on which heads, how its findings are recorded without a GitHub review, and what "reopens" an adjudication are all unstated, so the comparative-claim gates reference evidence that cannot be produced as written. Specify the control's mechanism, or drop the comparative path and keep only the descriptive record.

findings.title: Precision-evidence matching requirement is unsatisfiable as written
findings.body: AC15(d) requires "the paired precision evidence AC9 defines on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count" and the consistency matrix's claim-admissibility row repeats it "as the real-pull-request comparison". AC9's precision evidence is fixture-based: a real-pull-request head set has no fixture version and no precision-fixture target, so read literally no comparative recall claim can ever be admissible, which the matrix's own example (only model identity is policed against the claimed heads) does not intend. Say explicitly which elements must match the two precision arms to each other (target, fixture version, sample count, per AC9) and which must match the claimed heads (model identity, category-list version, effective sweep configuration), and align the matrix row.

findings.title: AC20 forces finding content into logs, which must never carry credential values
findings.body: AC20 requires "Every finding published by a sweep pass" to appear in the per-category pass record "on the surfaces AC1 assigns to the pass's outcome", and AC1 assigns the logs for every case; Operational Visibility says "Logs never record credential values" (line 945) and AC14 forbids quality evidence containing usable credential values. Findings for the swept credential-pattern category are precisely those likely to quote a credential, and the spec never says whether the record carries finding text, location, or an identifier only. Specify that the record carries non-secret references (path/line/identifier) rather than quoted credential text so AC20 and the no-secrets rule can both hold, and state it in Operational Visibility's per-category record description.

findings.title: AC11 demands a cost comparison the spec says cannot be made
findings.body: AC11 requires the cost evidence to be "compare[d] ... against the recorded per-pull-request convergence figures", while Use Case 4 states that "The 2026-09-23 cost baseline contains no Ronda pass cost at all — Ronda accounted for none of the Actions time in that window — so the sweep-off control run is the only same-shape cost comparison available". The acceptance criterion therefore requires a comparison whose admissible form and content are undefined, against figures the spec itself says are not same-shape. Make the testable output the paired per-run sweep-on vs sweep-off differences AC11 already defines, and say explicitly that the baseline figures may only be cited as context, not compared as a cost effect.

findings.title: Cost ceiling: "necessary for a default flip" vs "only two tests gate it"
findings.body: Use Case 4 says "A ceiling becomes necessary only if the sweep is later proposed as the default for adopting repositories", while the business rule at lines 752-759 says of the default flip that "only two tests are gating": evidence recorded and no precision regression, with no cost ceiling defined or required, and the Deferred Decisions trigger for a cost ceiling is "Only if the sweep is proposed as the default". Clarify whether a default flip requires the cost-ceiling decision first (as "becomes necessary" implies) or not (as "only two tests" implies).

findings.title: AC6 hard-codes five categories, making the first list revision fail the criterion
findings.body: AC6 requires that "The swept list holds exactly the five categories in Statuses / Enum Values" and that the excluded entries are exactly the recorded set, but Use Case 2 steps 4-5, AC7's revision history, and the business rule "Changing the sweep category list is a human decision" all treat the list as revisable. The first legitimate revision makes AC6 false, so the acceptance criterion cannot survive the behaviour the spec requires. State AC6 against the current list version — every candidate swept or explicitly excluded with a recorded rationale, exactly one current version, no candidate undecided — and keep the concrete five-category content as the initial list in Statuses / Enum Values.

findings.title: Consistency-matrix mirror-surface pointers cite the wrong sites
findings.body: The sweep-enablement row cites "Business rule 'Whether the sweep is enabled is read from the effective operator configuration value' (~106)", but that text is in Use Case 1 Considerations (starting line 120) and the Business Rules section contains no enablement rule. The same row set cites "the per-category pass record business rule (~541)", while the per-category business rule begins at line 616. findings.title: Add the required Document Quality Gate log, including the Matrix coherence preflight row
