findings.title: AC6 freezes the list at exactly five categories, contradicting the revision workflow
findings.body: AC6 requires that "The swept list holds exactly the five categories in Statuses / Enum Values, and the excluded entries are the seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds, the planted-proof evidence theme, spec-AC-compliance, and per-finding resolution". That is a permanent invariant on a snapshot. Use Case 2 step 4 explicitly permits "adding, removing, or reordering categories", AC7 requires a revision history, and the Business Rules state that changing the list is a human decision. After the first permitted revision — or after a later candidate is excluded — AC6 fails as written, so an implementer cannot tell whether AC6 is a one-time acceptance of the initial list or a standing constraint that forbids revision. Scope AC6 to the initial version (e.g. "the initial recorded list version contains exactly the five categories… and its excluded entries are…") and let the general record requirements (AC4, AC5, AC7) govern later versions.

findings.title: Whether a cost ceiling is needed before flipping the sweep default is answered two ways
findings.body: Use Case 4 says "No cost ceiling applies to this feature: cost is reported, not capped. A ceiling becomes necessary only if the sweep is later proposed as the default for adopting repositories (see Deferred Decisions)", and the Deferred Decisions row for "A cost ceiling per sweep pass" is triggered by exactly that event. But the Business Rules say that "only two tests are gating for that later decision: recall, variance, precision, and cost evidence must all have been recorded, and precision must not have regressed", and that "No recall-improvement target, variance ceiling, or cost ceiling is defined, so recall, variance, and cost results are reported evidence … they do not pass or fail a default-enablement gate". So it is undecided whether a ceiling must exist before the default flips. Pick one: either the ceiling is a precondition of the default change (and say so in the Business Rules and the Deferred Decisions trigger), or it is merely a decision that may be taken then (and remove "becomes necessary" from Use Case 4).

findings.title: The claim that two adjudicators derive identical sweep membership is untestable
findings.body: AC15(d) (restated in the Use Case 6 Considerations and the real-PR Business Rule) asserts that "two adjudicators reading the same closed cohort derive the same membership, since a defect either matches a recorded category or does not", and makes admissibility depend on membership being recorded before the claim is read. The matching rule is only "matched against the recorded category list's categories and their recorded failure shapes (AC4)", and those failure shapes are one-sentence prose with overlapping scope — e.g. a credential guard that continues when its config cannot be loaded fits both `credential-pattern-gap` ("a credential … the guard's pattern does not match") and `guard-fails-open` ("a check that continues when its input cannot be loaded"). Use Case 1 also states that a finding may fit more than one category. With no decidable test or tie-break, the determinism claim is an unstated assumption and the denominator cannot be verified by a reader. Either define a decidable matching test (for example, first-match by list order, or a required single primary category per defect) or drop the determinism claim and specify how a genuine disagreement is resolved.

findings.title: The "recorded but not published" sweep-off control has no defined mechanism and collides with AC2
findings.body: Use Case 6 requires, for any comparative real-PR claim, "a sweep-off review of the same pull request heads, with the same model and configuration apart from the sweep setting, recorded but not published, covering the whole closed cohort". No section defines how such a run is produced. AC2 says that "whenever the existing review flow reaches publication for that head SHA, Ronda publishes exactly one review per head SHA", and AC18 says a disabled sweep "reproduces the non-sweep review behavior … same single review per head SHA". So a sweep-off pass over already-reviewed heads either publishes (breaking one-review-per-head-SHA) or needs a publish-suppression mode the spec never introduces — and Out of Scope bars changing "review output contract, check-run behavior, draft-skip behavior, supersede behavior, or trigger behavior". State how the control run is executed (benchmark/replay against the recorded heads, a dry-run mode, something else), where its findings are recorded, and confirm it does not publish.

findings.title: Matrix lists whitespace-only enablement as an off outcome while AC18 makes it defer
findings.body: The `Sweep enablement resolution (AC18)` row defines its input as "the value from the highest-precedence source that supplies a non-empty value" and lists as an outcome "Off — absent, empty, or whitespace-only (no record)", with the example covering only "An empty value at a higher-precedence source defers to the next source". AC18 instead says "A value that is empty or contains only whitespace counts as absent", i.e. a whitespace-only value at a higher-precedence source is treated as absent and defers to the next source. Whitespace is a non-empty string, so the two readings disagree: with whitespace at the highest-precedence source and a recognized on value below it, the matrix yields Off and AC18 yields On. Align the matrix input and example with AC18 (say "non-empty after trimming" or add the whitespace example).

findings.title: The counted cohort is undefined for heads whose sweep pass published no review
findings.body: Use Case 6 step 1 defines the eligible cohort as "the pull requests that carried a sweep-enabled Ronda review under the current category list version whose pass completed by a recorded cutoff", and the Business Rules define a sweep-enabled review as "a review whose pass actually ran the sweep and reported a category list version as used". AC1 says a pass superseded before publication "publishes no review and writes no check run, so its record is on the logs only" and Use Case 1 says such a pass still owes a per-category record. So a head whose only sweep pass was superseded (or which failed terminally after review execution, where the finding result exists but nothing was published) carried a sweep pass but no review: the spec never says whether that head is in the cohort, whether it counts toward ten, or whether it alone promotes the tier from `fixture_only`. The word "completed" is also undefined against AC1's completion/terminal-failure taxonomy. State explicitly that a pass which publishes no review neither enters the cohort nor promotes the tier (or the opposite), and replace "whose pass completed" with the AC1 term.

findings.title: "Clean result" carries two meanings and AC10's "publishes a clean result" is undefined
findings.body: AC10 says a pass that finds nothing "publishes a clean result", but nothing defines a clean result for a review pass, and whether a zero-finding pass publishes a review at all is left to "the existing review flow" (which AC10 then carves out). Elsewhere "clean result" means a pull request whose compared reviewers reported no findings and which is confirmed by the recorded same-head external review (`clean_agreement`, Use Case 6 and the `real_pr_provisional` row). Use distinct wording — e.g. "a review with no findings" for the pass and "confirmed clean adjudication" for the cohort — and say in AC10 exactly what the sweep pass emits when it finds nothing.

findings.title: Decision-gate matrix mirror-surface pointers do not resolve
findings.body: The Mirror surfaces column cites "Business rule 'Whether the sweep is enabled is read from the effective operator configuration value' (~106)" and "Business rule 'If the current category list cannot be read…' (~120)". The Business Rules section contains no such titled rules; those sentences live in Use Case 1's Considerations, and the anchors are inconsistent with the ~541 anchor used for the per-category-record business rule. Cite the actual section and heading (e.g. "Use Case 1 → Considerations, sweep enablement value" and "Business Rules, 'When the sweep is enabled and the current category list cannot be read…'") so a reader can check that each mirror states the same rule.

findings.title: Add the per-rule Plan authoring rigor outcome record
findings.body: The plan has no `Plan authoring rigor` outcome record at all: none of the six canonical rules (Sampling an external output distribution; One normative statement per fact; Counts of codebase artifacts; Independent verification of existence claims; Expectations at the composed call site; A conditional obligation names its scope) is recorded as `Satisfied` / `Not applicable` / `Unsatisfied` with repository-derived evidence at the recorded revision, and there is no reasoned `Not applicable` anywhere. Several rules plainly fire: Rule 3 on the enumerated counts (`13` seeded defects, `1` precision fixture, the five swept categories, the 8-row cost table), Rule 4 on 'no sweep code exists yet' and 'sweep artifact absent', Rule 6 on the many 'only when…' / 'emitted only once…' obligations. A blanket not-applicable entry would therefore be wrong. REVIEW.md's Group H makes a missing outcome record blocking; add the section and tie each firing rule to its evidence.

findings.title: Restore AC1's review-execution boundary
findings.body: Rule 1 here (and rule 2, Testing Strategy scenario 5, and the `Pass-outcome surface assignment` matrix row) moves AC1's boundary from 'reads the changed files and runs the review' to 'issues the review request'. AC1 draws its exclusion at failures `before` that point and names its examples as 'a missing model credential, a config load error, or a deadline abort or GitHub error raised before the changed files are read'; it then puts 'a model or GitHub error raised after the changed files are read' explicitly in the terminal-failure case that records reached categories on the logs. AC18 and AC19 likewise say their records are emitted by every pass that reaches review execution and withheld only from passes that end before it. So on the plan's own premise that the authoritative-document fetch sits after `readChangedFiles` and before `deps.model.complete`, a sweep-enabled pass that fails there has reached review execution and owes its degraded record on the logs (its check run is the failure run) — yet the plan states it emits 'no sweep record at all, not even a degraded one' and encodes that in scenario 5 as 'matching the same-throw-without-sweep case byte for byte'. Either move the boundary back to the changed-files read or record the reinterpretation as an open question against AC1/AC19 rather than as settled behaviour.

findings.title: Include the Document Quality Gate log in the PR description
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required `Document Quality Gate` log is missing entirely; per REVIEW.md that is an important finding by default. It also matters here that the plan carries its own stateful contract (the Decision-gate matrix plus the three per-category outcome values and their surface-assignment rules), so the log must include a populated `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary — not a `Not applicable — no stateful contract` row, which would itself be blocking.

findings.title: Carry finding-to-category attribution in the pass record
findings.body: `SweepPassRecord` is defined as 'categories array + `uncategorizedFindingCount`', and step 11's benchmark output reuses that type. Rule 3 meanwhile says 'a finding matching one or more categories is recorded against every category it matches' — but no field in the record (or in the benchmark output shape, or in the check-run renderer's 'one line per category with its outcome, plus the uncategorized finding count') can hold a finding. Consequences: AC9 requires each sweep-on unexpected finding to be attributed to the category (or categories, or uncategorized) recorded for it, and AC20 requires every published finding to appear in the record either against a category or as uncategorized; a bare count satisfies neither, and smoke-test Step 9's attribution expectation cannot be met. Add the matched findings' identity to the record so rule 3 and the type agree.

findings.title: Bound the matchTerms classifier's specificity
findings.body: Rule 3 makes categorisation a literal lowercase substring match of each category's `matchTerms` against `title + body`, with `matchTerms` 'drawn from the category's failureShape wording', and the Seed Data row for the first seed proposes 'matchTerms over "head", "api", "evidence"/"inference"'. On any non-trivial review those tokens occur in most findings, so nearly every finding would be attributed to `pr-head-push-order`, `uncategorizedFindingCount` would stay near zero, and the AC9 attribution and the AC15(d) category-membership evidence built on this record become meaningless — the opposite of the 'objective match' the spec needs. The plan neither bounds term specificity nor forbids common-word terms, and scenario 2's tests (one match, two matches, none, case-insensitivity, determinism) never test discrimination on realistic finding text. Add a specificity rule and a negative/realistic-text test, or state how the resulting record stays interpretable.

findings.title: Off is not a degraded path that carries a record
findings.body: The Summary says 'every degraded path (off, unrecognized value, unreadable/empty/malformed list) degrades to the existing non-sweep review with the spec-mandated record and no failure'. AC18 makes an absent, empty, whitespace-only, or recognized-off value produce no record at all, and the plan says so itself in the `load-config.ts` bullet ('absent, empty, or whitespace-only → off, not supplied (one case, no record)') and in both decision-matrix rows (`Off — recognized off value (no record)`). Only the unrecognized non-empty value and the unreadable/empty/malformed list carry records. Reword the Summary so a reader cannot implement an enablement record for the ordinary off case.

findings.title: Fix the snapshot step cross-reference
findings.body: The runbook says the original-thirteen snapshot was 'created in implementation step 9'. In the plan, step 9 is `Workflow + example config`; the snapshot is created in step 10 (`Fixture seeds`), which the plan's own step 11 refers to as 'the step-10 snapshot'. Correct the reference (or renumber consistently across both documents); as written, the runbook points the operator at the wrong step.

findings.title: Scope the AC14 credential scan to authenticating values
findings.body: Scenario 7's first assertion 'fails if any value matches a real-credential shape (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `ghs_…`, …)' contradicts AC14, which does not prohibit and AC13 positively requires non-functional credential-*shaped* fixture data: every acceptable placeholder (`sk-placeholder`, `ghp_test_only`) matches those shapes, so the test as specified fails on the very data the feature must ship. The second assertion (each seed's credential-shaped string is declared non-functional — a `forbiddenValue` the existing redaction path handles, or a non-authenticating placeholder) is the right discriminator; make the shape scan an inventory that is then checked against those declarations, with only undeclared/authenticating values failing. Separately, the parenthetical 'a JWTs three-dot form' misdescribes a JWT (three dot-separated segments = two dots), so a pattern written to that wording would not match a JWT.

findings.title: Specify the seed patch targets
findings.body: All five seed rows give their target as '`src/benchmark/git-history.ts` or similar', '`src/benchmark/output.ts` or similar', and so on, and no Verification Log check establishes that `src/benchmark/` or any of those files exists. A seeded defect is a patch that must apply to a real file, so the implementer must guess both the target file and whether a new one is to be created — exactly the guessing the checklist forbids, and an unverified existence claim under Rule 4. Name the exact file and the shape of each patch, or add a Verification Log line establishing the available target paths.

findings.title: Back the hardcoded line numbers with a verification entry
findings.body: The plan cites source line ranges that no Verification Log check produced: `src/cli/review-pr.ts` L81–90, `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` L224–233, `tests/integration/review-pass.test.ts` L84/L223/L304, `src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts:475-489`, `tests/unit/cli/recall-benchmark.test.ts` L26 and L243, `tests/unit/webhook/webhook-job.test.ts` L111, and `.github/workflows/ronda-review.yml` L134–145 (also carrying the precedence claim). REVIEW.md classes numeric cross-references that cannot be confirmed against source files or Verification Log output as important; they also hide a missed call site when they drift. Either record the query that produced each number in the Verification Log or replace the numbers with file + symbol.

findings.title: Plan the benchmark's log surface
findings.body: This bullet asserts that for a sweep-on benchmark run the per-category record is 'in this output and the logs (AC1)', but step 11 specifies only the JSON summary / `--output-file` output, and scenario 6 asserts only the summary shape (record present sweep-on, absent sweep-off, identity blocks, `--runs 2`). AC1 and the `Pass-outcome surface assignment` row require the record on a completed benchmark run's own output *and* its logs, since a benchmark publishes no check run. Add the log emission and its assertion to step 11 / scenario 6, or drop the log claim from this bullet.

findings.title: Resolve the conditional documentation entries
findings.body: Documentation Updates leaves its listed targets undecided: `docs/testing/README.md` 'if that file's conventions require it', and `docs/project/1-business-domain.md` / `3-software-architecture.md` 'only if those docs enumerate every review mode; verify against their current content during implementation' (the `AGENTS.md` entry is likewise conditional on a script that may not be added). The checklist requires documentation updates to be listed or intentionally declared unnecessary; 'add it if it turns out to be needed' leaves the reviewer unable to check coverage and is the vague-wording case REVIEW.md calls important. Decide now from the current file contents, or declare each unnecessary with the reason.

findings.title: Cite how the loader resolves the artifact path
findings.body: The bullet guarantees the list is 'Loaded by absolute path from the Ronda checkout — never fetched from the reviewed head', and `loadSweepList` takes no argument in production, but no mechanism is given for resolving 'the Ronda checkout' (module-relative path, `process.cwd()`, packaged asset root). `process.cwd()` resolves inside the reviewed repository for a local run and arbitrarily for the webhook process, which would break both the guarantee and AC19's degrade reason; a distribution that excludes `docs/` would make the sweep degrade on every pass. Name the resolution mechanism and add an assertion that a run from an unrelated working directory still loads the repository artifact.

findings.title: Reconcile the default vocabulary claim
findings.body: The Summary describes `default` as 'an explicit `default` alias for `off`' (an addition), while this row records `default` as already 'recognized (durability only)' and the `load-config.ts` bullet says the sweep parser must recognize it because `parseBooleanFlag` does not. AC18 requires the same vocabulary as the durability switch, so say once whether `default` is part of the existing vocabulary or an extension, and make the Summary and this row agree.

findings.title: Make the workflow verification executable
findings.body: Step 9's verification is '`yaml` syntax of the workflow is valid (the existing CI workflow lints or a careful read)' — a verification that states its own uncertainty, so it cannot be confirmed by reading the plan or the output. Replace it with a command whose output can be read (the repo's existing workflow/yaml lint) or state plainly that only a manual read is available.

findings.title: Decide the optional precision fixture
findings.body: 'the new credential seed's clean counterpart may be added if the developer judges it needed — not required by AC9' leaves the precision evidence set undecided. Adding it later changes the fixture version/sample count that AC9 and AC8 require to match the recall runs, so decide now: either add it as a required seed or state that `harmless-session-refactor` alone is the precision target.

findings.title: Rename the seed so it does not reuse a category identifier
findings.body: The new seed id `guard-fails-open` is byte-identical to the swept category identifier `guard-fails-open` (the other seeds are distinct, e.g. `credential-pattern-gap-camel` vs `credential-pattern-gap`). Seed ids and category identifiers are different namespaces that both surface in the benchmark output and the per-category record, so a shared string invites reading one as the other. Rename the seed (for example `guard-fails-open-unloaded-input`).

errorMessage: Model response was empty or whitespace-only
Model response was empty or whitespace-only

findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log to the PR description
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so this plan PR carries no `Document Quality Gate` log and no `Matrix coherence preflight` row. The plan contains a stateful contract — the `Decision-gate matrix (plan-time classification)` and the AC18 precedence rules in the `load-config.ts` bullet — so a reasoned `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary is required, not a `Not applicable`. A missing log is an important readiness defect by default; add the current log before requesting human review.

findings.title: Add the per-rule plan-authoring-rigor outcome record
findings.body: The plan carries no per-rule outcome record for `docs/workflow/development-workflow/plan-authoring-rigor-rules.md` — no `Satisfied` / `Not applicable` / `Unsatisfied` entry per rule with evidence at the recorded revision `def04bd`. Several rules plainly fire here: Rule 1 (the classifier design depends on the wording of model-produced finding text), Rule 3 and 4 (counts and existence claims such as "13 seeded defects", "no sweep code exists yet", "`grep ... | wc -l` = 0", "comparison records exist"), and Rule 6 (conditional obligations such as "reported only where the pass's check-run write produced a review-outcome check run"). Per Group H in the canonical file, a missing outcome record (and a missing rationale where a rule is marked not applicable) is blocking.

findings.title: Put `sweep-did-not-run` and the unrecognized-enablement record on the check-run surface too
findings.body: Spec Operational Visibility says the per-category record, the `sweep-did-not-run` record, and the unrecognized-enablement record are all carried "on those same surfaces" — the surfaces AC1 assigns to the pass's outcome, i.e. the check-run output wherever the pass's own write produced a review-outcome check run, plus the logs. The plan's only check-run change is `CheckRunOutputInput.sweep?: SweepPassRecord` (the per-category record), and both other records are described as log events only (`run-review-pass.ts` steps 1 and 2), with the readability and enablement matrix rows (lines 132–133) naming no record surface. The runbook contradicts this: Step 3 tells the tester to "inspect the logs and check-run output" for the unrecognized case. Add the two records to the check-run rendering and to the matrix rows, or record explicitly why the check-run surface is out of scope for them.

findings.title: Constrain the finding-to-category matcher before it feeds evidence
findings.body: `classifyFindings` attributes a finding to every category whose recorded `matchTerms` appear as literal substrings in the lowercased `title + "\n" + body`, and those terms are only "lowercase literal substrings drawn from the category's `failureShape` wording" (the Seed Data row suggests terms like "head", "api", "evidence"/"inference"). Nothing requires a term to be discriminating, so a finding that incidentally mentions a common word records `produced_findings` for a category that produced nothing, while a genuine finding phrased with an inflection (`credentials` vs `credential`, which no stemming can bridge) records `produced_none`. This record is what AC9's per-category precision attribution and AC15(d)'s "within the sweep's claim" membership are read off, and AC15(d) says a misrecording carries no membership. Specify a discriminating term set (or a stronger matcher) and add a test that an incidental mention is not attributed. The `Parser-risk addendum`'s "Not applicable — ... not text scanning" also understates the design: it samples the wording of externally produced text.

findings.title: `matchTerms` is neither an AC4 field nor an AC19 malformed case
findings.body: AC4 fixes the per-category fields (identifier, display label, description, failure shape, evidence source, finding-instance count) and AC19 defines the malformed cases as missing or out-of-domain values among those fields, duplicate identifiers, zero categories, and no identifiable list version. The plan adds `matchTerms` as a required non-empty array and makes a missing/empty one a validation failure, so a list that satisfies AC19 exactly but derives its terms elsewhere would be rejected and the pass would silently degrade to non-sweep. Either keep `matchTerms` optional (deriving terms from `failureShape` at load time) or record it explicitly as a deliberate extension of the AC4/AC19 contract.

findings.title: Plan the operator's readiness declaration for the extended fixture
findings.body: AC17 requires documentation to state three things: that the seeded benchmark is not a gate until the AC12/AC13 seeds exist, that the operator may declare the extended fixture ready to serve as the basis of a regression gate with the declaration recorded (Use Case 5 step 4), and that what a restored gate rejects is deferred. This item and the runbook's Step 12 carry only the first and third. No step says where the readiness declaration is recorded or who makes it, so the middle clause of AC17 is unplanned; add it to `sweep-effect-evidence.md` requirements and to Step 12's expected result.

findings.title: Replace conditional documentation steps with decided ones
findings.body: `docs/testing/README.md` is to be indexed "if that file's conventions require it" (line 159); `docs/project/1-business-domain.md` and `3-software-architecture.md` change "only if those docs enumerate every review mode; verify against their current content during implementation" (line 161); `AGENTS.md` gets a conditional npm-script row (line 160). This is the "update as needed" pattern: the implementer must guess, and the reviewer cannot tell whether the step was done. Read those files at plan time and state the outcome (change, or no change with the reason), as the plan does for the loader and renderer edits.

findings.title: Preserve an addressable original-fixture version for AC8's control
findings.body: Step 9 adds the five seeds to the existing `tests/fixtures/recall-benchmark/manifest.json` and `patches.json`, and step 10 (line 216) and runbook Step 8 then run the original-thirteen control by "pointing `--manifest` and `--patches` at the original fixture version". No such file set is planned: after step 9 the original manifest and patches exist only in git history at `def04bd`, and nothing tells the operator to materialize them or commits a frozen copy. AC8 makes that repeated original-fixture control mandatory (≥5 runs per configuration), so the campaign cannot be executed as written without inventing a mechanism. Add a step that commits a frozen original-fixture copy (or records the base revision and the exact command to materialize it) and point the control commands and runbook Step 8 at it.

findings.title: Verify or add the benchmark CLI flags the campaign commands use
findings.body: Step 10 adds exactly three flags (`--sweep-mode`, `--runs`, `--output-file`), yet the same bullet and runbook Step 8 also invoke `--manifest`, `--patches`, `--precision-response-file`, and describe `--quality` composition on `src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts`. The Verification Log's benchmark row records only that `runRecallBenchmark` / `runPrecisionFixture` exist and print a JSON summary; it does not confirm these argument names or that a precision fixture is runnable from the CLI. If they do not exist, most campaign commands fail. Either add them to the enumerated flag work (with parsing and tests) or record their current names and a Verification Log query that shows them.

findings.title: Name the seed target files instead of "or similar"
findings.body: Every new seed's location is written as a path "or similar" (`src/benchmark/git-history.ts`, `src/benchmark/output.ts`, `src/benchmark/guard.ts`, `src/benchmark/records.ts`, `src/benchmark/credentials.ts`), and the state-reconstruction row's `matchTerms` are left as "head", "api", "evidence"/"inference". The implementer must guess which file each seeded defect lives in, whether those paths exist in the fixture's target or in this repository, and how `patches.json` applies the patch. Read the existing fixture's shape (target repo, patch format, manifest fields) at plan time and specify each seed concretely, including the exact `harderThan` value and canonical baseline form.

findings.title: Complete the evidence-tier row with the count-restart rule
findings.body: The spec's Evidence-tier transitions make a list revision at `real_pr_provisional` leave the tier unchanged and restart the counted pull requests at zero, and leave `fixture_only` unchanged on revision; a revision is also named as one cause of demotion from `real_pr_measured`. The plan's row lists only the promotions/demotions plus "all other combinations unchanged", so the count-restart rule is missing from the one row the plan says the implementation and `sweep-real-pr-evidence.md` "must reproduce exactly". Add the restart and the `fixture_only`-on-revision outcome.

findings.title: The withdrawal mitigation rests on a false premise
findings.body: The row claims "the sweep writes only metadata, so a withdrawn sweep leaves no residue on any pull request" and that a config-only withdrawal "restores the exact pre-feature pass — same prompt, same summary, same check run". The sweep's whole purpose is to change what the prompt asks for, and AC3 has it write an activation-and-version line into every published review summary, so a sweep-enabled pass does leave sweep content on the pull request (and changes findings). Restate the mitigation as: passes run after the withdrawal are identical to pre-feature passes, while already-published reviews keep their sweep summary line and sweep-influenced findings.

findings.title: Map AC10 to an actual test case
findings.body: Testing Strategy scenario 5 lists AC10 among the criteria it maps, but none of its cases covers a sweep-enabled pass that finds nothing for every category: it covers findings present, malformed list, unrecognized value, terminal failure, and pre-review skips. Scenario 7's "unmatched by the clean precision fixture" tests a fixture response against the classifier, not that a clean sweep pass publishes a clean result and manufactures no per-category finding (AC10, including "A pass whose only findings are uncategorized ... is not clean"). Add the pass-level clean case (fixture-response mode) to the scenario list and to the runbook.

findings.title: Name the category-list version and effective review configuration in the evidence
findings.body: AC9 requires the committed evidence to record the category-list version and the effective review configuration (review prompt, inference parameters, immutable model version) the runs used, and runbook Step 9 asks for them. Step 11's enumeration of what `sweep-effect-evidence.md` must contain — per-run recall, lowest/highest, population standard deviation, per-defect counts, sample count, immutable model version, reviewed target, timestamps, fixture version, original-thirteen subset, non-comparable label, precision result, cost figures — omits both and reads as the complete list. Add both fields so the plan and runbook agree and a later recall claim can be paired to its heads.

findings.title: Drop the per-category `version` from `SweepCategory`
findings.body: The `review-pass.types.ts` bullet gives `SweepCategory` a `version` field, but the artifact's per-category fields (AC4) and the loader's validation carry the version only at list level (`SweepCategoryList.version`), and the prompt section renders only identifier, display label, description, and failure shape. As written the loader has to invent a value for a field nothing defines; align the type with the artifact.

findings.title: The Approach sentence says the plain off path records something
findings.body: The Approach lists "off" among the degraded paths that run "with the spec-mandated record", but AC18 and the plan's own `load-config.ts` bullet make absent, empty, whitespace-only, and recognized-off values produce no record at all; the unrecognized non-empty value is the only off case with a record. Reword so the summary does not suggest a record for the ordinary off path.

findings.title: Missing Document Quality Gate log and Matrix coherence preflight row
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so there is no `Document Quality Gate` log. The plan contains a Decision-gate matrix and precedence rules, so the log must carry a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary (or a reasoned `Not applicable` only if the check genuinely does not apply). Add the current log to the PR description; without it the plan cannot pass the repository's plan-stage gate.

findings.title: Add the plan-authoring-rigor per-rule outcome record
findings.body: The plan has no per-rule outcome record for `docs/workflow/development-workflow/plan-authoring-rigor-rules.md`. All six rules fire here: Rule 1 (the sweep classifier's behaviour depends on the wording of externally produced model finding text), Rule 2 (the plan asserts facts throughout), Rule 3 (13 seeded defects, one precision fixture, five seeds, enumerated config literal sites), Rule 4 ('no sweep code exists yet', 'loadConfig already carries the fields', 'artifact absent'), Rule 5 (`buildReviewPrompt` gains an input and has more than one consumer — run-review-pass and the benchmark), and Rule 6 (conditional obligations such as 'loaded at pass time, never from the reviewed head'). Record the outcome (`Satisfied`/`Not applicable`/`Unsatisfied`) with repository-derived evidence at `def04bd` for each rule in the plan document.

findings.title: Key not_determined off result existence, not publication
findings.body: Step 4 keys `not_determined` off 'where the failure precedes the review becoming public'. Spec AC1 says not-determined 'belongs only to that case: a failure after review execution but before the review result exists'. A failure of the review publication call — or any failure after the model response is parsed — happens when the review result exists, and AC1 requires the ordinary `produced_findings`/`produced_none` values on the logs (the check run is the failure check run, so no check-run output). As written, a category whose result is known would be recorded as not determined. Redraw the boundary at result existence rather than publication, and extend the runbook's Step 6 (which only exercises a model-call failure) to cover a publication-call failure.

findings.title: Carry the degraded-sweep records on the AC1 check-run surface
findings.body: Steps 1–2 put `sweep_enablement_unrecognized` and `sweep-did-not-run` on the logs only, and `CheckRunOutputInput` gains only `sweep?: SweepPassRecord`, so the check-run output can never carry either record. Spec AC18 requires the unrecognized record 'on the surfaces AC1 assigns to the pass's outcome', and Operational Visibility says both records are 'carried on those same surfaces'. A degraded pass that reaches review execution and publishes a review produces a review-outcome check run, so AC1 assigns these records to the check-run output and the logs. Add a field for these records on the check-run output and place them on both surfaces (runbook Steps 3–4 should assert the check-run surface too).

findings.title: Fix the failure-shape matchTerms classifier and its validator coupling
findings.body: `matchTerms` are 'lowercase literal substrings drawn from the category's `failureShape` wording' and the classifier in step 3 matches them as literal substrings of the finding's lowercased title + body. Failure shapes are abstract prose (e.g. `Which commits were ever branch heads, inferred from a response that does not establish it`); model findings are concrete sentences, so this matcher will rarely hit, driving every category to `produced_none` and every finding to uncategorized. That guts AC1/AC20 attribution and the AC15(d) membership the pass record is meant to fix. Separately, `matchTerms` is a required field in the validator but is not an AC4/AC19 field: a Use Case 2 revision that omits it makes the whole list 'malformed', so the sweep silently degrades to `sweep-did-not-run`. Specify terms (or a rule) that reflect finding wording, test against realistic model output, decide the consequence of a missing `matchTerms`, and correct the Parser-risk addendum's 'not text scanning' rationale — enumerate empty/missing title or body and word-boundary false positives (`head` matching `header`).

findings.title: Name the mechanism that keeps the list off the reviewed head
findings.body: The artifact bullet says the list is 'Loaded from the repository root at pass time — never fetched from the reviewed head', and production calls `loadSweepList()` with no path. In the Actions ingress Ronda runs from the reviewed repository's checkout (`ronda-review.yml` maps inputs to env; nothing in the Verification Log shows a separate Ronda checkout), so resolving `docs/testing/ronda/sweep-categories.json` from that working tree is reading the reviewed head — a PR could change its own category list. No mechanism (pinned ref, separate checkout, packaged artifact) is named for the guarantee, and the loader's base-path resolution is left for the implementer to guess. State the resolution mechanism and add a test that a head modifying the artifact does not change the list used.

findings.title: Preserve the original-thirteen fixture for the AC8 control
findings.body: Step 9 adds the five seeds to the same `tests/fixtures/recall-benchmark/manifest.json` and `patches.json`, after which no 'original fixture version' exists, yet step 10's campaign leg and runbook Step 8 run the control 'with `--manifest`/`--patches` pointing at the original fixture version'. AC8 requires the repeated original-thirteen control. Specify how the original fixture is preserved (a committed copy, or a pinned revision plus extraction procedure); otherwise the control cannot be run as planned.

findings.title: Emit cost figures for the sweep-off benchmark arm
findings.body: The `src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts` bullet makes the cost fields conditional on the sweep input ('when present … the returned summary carries … model-call count and elapsed time per pass'), so a `--sweep-mode off` run would carry no cost figures. AC11 requires model calls and elapsed time per pass for both configurations, and step 10's output shape gives them unconditionally. Make per-run model-call count and elapsed time unconditional, and reconcile the 'Default 1 keeps today's single-run output identical' claim with those added fields.

findings.title: State the post-seed AC17 gate status
findings.body: The Documentation Updates item and runbook Step 12 reduce AC17 to 'the seeded benchmark is not a regression gate until the AC12/AC13 seeds exist' plus the deferred gate contract. AC17 also requires the documentation to state that the operator may declare the extended fixture ready as a gate basis once the seeds exist — and this same change adds the seeds, so the 'until the seeds exist' wording is stale at ship time. State the post-seed status (seeds present; fixture may be declared ready; what a restored gate rejects is deferred).

findings.title: Verify the RondaConfig literal sites against the codebase
findings.body: The 'Verified sites' list cites `src/cli/review-pr.ts` L81–90, `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` L224–233, and `tests/integration/review-pass.test.ts` L84/L223/L304, but the Verification Log has no command that reads those files or lines (only `load-config.ts` and workflow L134–145). The claim that these are the construction sites 'every full `RondaConfig` literal' reaches is a completeness assertion over an unverified enumeration. Add Verification Log commands (e.g. a grep for the literals) recording the exact sites, or mark the list as indicative.

findings.title: Verify campaign CLI flags and account for generated output files
findings.body: The campaign commands rely on `--manifest`, `--patches`, and `--precision-response-file`, none of which the Benchmark runner Verification Log row confirms (`runRecallBenchmark`/`runPrecisionFixture` build prompts via `buildReviewPrompt` and print one JSON summary). If any flag does not exist, runbook Steps 8–9 fail. Also, `--output-file docs/testing/ronda/sweep-{off,on}-extended.json` writes generated JSON into the docs tree while the evidence doc is 'assembled from those files', but the plan never says whether those outputs are committed or temporary. Verify/label the existing flags and declare the output files' disposition.

findings.title: Cover the webhook's deployment-wide enablement scope
findings.body: AC18 scopes enablement per repository for the Actions ingress and deployment-wide where the webhook resolves one process-wide operator configuration. The plan adds the workflow input but never states or tests the webhook's deployment-wide behavior; `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` appears only as a `RondaConfig` literal site. State that the webhook resolves the same process-wide value (no repository-keyed source) and cover it in the smoke runbook or unit tests.

findings.title: Enforce AC7's version-never-reused rule
findings.body: AC7 requires that a version value 'is never reused'. The validator only requires the current version to be a non-blank scalar string compared by exact equality ('exact-string-equality identity'); nothing rejects a revision that reuses `sweep-categories-v1` or any prior value, and the Use Case 2 operator revision procedure is not required to mint a new one. Add the never-reuse rule to the artifact/revision procedure and validate the current version against `revisionHistory`.

findings.title: Make SweepCategory.version consistent with the artifact
findings.body: `SweepCategory` is typed with a per-category `version`, but the artifact shape in Recorded artifacts gives categories only identifier/displayLabel/description/failureShape/evidenceSource/findingInstanceCount/matchTerms, and version lives on `SweepCategoryList`/the file. Implementation step 3 mentions only `matchTerms`. Drop `version` from `SweepCategory` or place it consistently.

findings.title: Replace the conditional documentation targets with a decision
findings.body: Two Documentation Updates targets stay conditional and unverifiable: `docs/testing/README.md` — 'index … if that file's conventions require it', and `docs/project/1-business-domain.md`/`3-software-architecture.md` — 'only if those docs enumerate every review mode; verify against their current content during implementation'. Replace with a definite decision (update, or not, with the reason) so the step is executable.

findings.title: Add the plan-authoring rigor per-rule outcome record
findings.body: The plan carries no per-rule outcome record for `plan-authoring-rigor-rules.md`. None of the six canonical rules is recorded with one of `Satisfied` / `Not applicable` / `Unsatisfied`, a rationale, and evidence at the recorded revision `def04bd`. At minimum Rule 3 (Counts of codebase artifacts — the Verification Log's "13 seeded defects", "Sample count: 5"), Rule 4 (Independent verification of existence claims — "no sweep code exists yet", "Sweep artifact absent"), Rule 6 (A conditional obligation names its scope — the many "only if"/"once" obligations) and Rule 1 (Sampling an external output distribution — classification of externally produced review prose) fire and need their evidence recorded. Per the canonical file's Group H a missing outcome record is blocking: put the record in the plan itself (not in PR comments), with a reasoned `Not applicable` wherever a rule does not fire.

findings.title: PR description has no Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required current `Document Quality Gate` log is missing. This plan also carries its own stateful contract — the "Decision-gate matrix (plan-time classification)" plus the explicit `RONDA_SWEEP_MODE` precedence rules — so the log must include a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary (or a reasoned `Not applicable`), not a bare "no stateful contract" entry. Add the log to the PR description with both rows before readiness is assessed.

findings.title: Degraded-path records are planned for the logs only
findings.body: `run-review-pass` rule 1 emits `sweep_enablement_unrecognized` as a log event, and rule 2 logs `sweep-did-not-run`; `src/core/summary.ts` only gives `CheckRunOutputInput` a `sweep?: SweepPassRecord`, and the enablement row of the decision matrix names no record surface for the off cases. But AC18 requires the unrecognized-enablement record "on the surfaces AC1 assigns to the pass's outcome", AC19 requires the sweep-did-not-run record, and Operational Visibility states both records "are carried on those same surfaces" — which, for a pass whose own check-run write produced a review-outcome check run, includes the check-run output. The smoke runbook already contradicts the plan: Step 3 (its line 75) tells the operator to inspect "the logs and check-run output" for the unrecognized record, which nothing in the plan ever writes there. Decide the surface and add the degraded records (and a display form that never reveals `sweepModeRaw`) to `buildCheckRunOutput`, or correct the spec reading, the matrix row, and the runbook together so they agree.

findings.title: `matchTerms` narrows AC19's malformed-list contract
findings.body: The loader's validation list adds a mandatory `matchTerms` field ("non-empty array of non-blank strings"), and Testing scenario 2 plus Smoke Step 4 list a missing/empty/non-string `matchTerms` as an "AC19 malformed shape". AC19 enumerates the malformed conditions and fixes the allowed domain for the AC4 fields (identifier, display label, description, failure shape, evidence source, finding-instance count, list version); `matchTerms` is not one of them. As written, a list that satisfies AC19 in full but omits `matchTerms` would be rejected, and every sweep-enabled pass would degrade to a non-sweep review. Either derive the match terms from the recorded `failureShape` at load time, or make the field optional, so the plan does not reject lists the spec calls well-formed.

findings.title: Classifier depends on an unstated wording assumption
findings.body: Rule 3 classifies a finding only when its lowercased `title + "\n" + body` contains one of the category's recorded `matchTerms` (drawn from the category's `failureShape` wording) as a literal substring. Nothing in the design makes the model's finding prose reuse that vocabulary, so a finding that genuinely belongs to a category but is worded in ordinary review language is recorded as uncategorized. That record then feeds AC9's attribution of sweep-on unexpected findings and AC15(d)'s "within the sweep's claim" membership, so the assumption propagates into the evidence. State the assumption and address it (for example, have the prompt section require the category identifier in each finding and classify from that, or document how misclassification is bounded), rather than asserting determinism alone.

findings.title: Code sample contradicts the post-publication failure rule
findings.body: The code sample comments that "on terminal failure after review execution, every category in it records not_determined (logs only)". `run-review-pass` rule 4 and the "Pass-outcome surface assignment" matrix row say the opposite for one branch: `not_determined` belongs only to a failure before the review result exists, and where the review is already public (`reviewPublished` / post-publication check-run write failures) the pass must record the ordinary `produced_findings`/`produced_none` values on the logs and record nothing as not determined. The illustrative sample points the implementer at the wrong branch; fix the comment to name both branches.

findings.title: No test covers the review-already-public failure branch
findings.body: Testing scenario 5 covers "terminal failure after review execution: `not_determined` on logs only" and Implementation Order step 7 lists "skip, pre-execution failure, post-execution failure, superseded, success, benchmark-style" — none of these is rule 4's second branch, where the review is already public and the pass must record the ordinary `produced_findings`/`produced_none` outcomes (plus whatever its own check-run write produced) and nothing as `not_determined`. The Risks table nevertheless claims "Unit tests enumerate every AC1 path (scenario 5)". Add the post-publication failure (and check-run-write-after-publication) case to scenario 5 and to step 7's verify list, or the risk mitigation is false.

findings.title: No implementation step owns the config-literal edits
findings.body: This bullet enumerates the `RondaConfig` construction sites that must gain the two new required fields (`src/cli/review-pr.ts` L81–90, `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` L224–233, `tests/unit/core/run-review-pass.test.ts` `createConfig`, `tests/integration/review-pass.test.ts` L84/L223/L304), but no Implementation Order step performs those edits: step 1 only adds the fields and the loader resolution, and step 3's Verify is "`npm run typecheck` clean" while the literals still lack `sweepMode`/`sweepModeRaw`. Move the edits into step 1 (or add a step before step 3) with its own verify, otherwise the ordering as written fails at step 3.

findings.title: Line-number references are not backed by the Verification Log
findings.body: The row asserts `.github/workflows/ronda-review.yml` L134–145 and the Backend section asserts `src/cli/review-pr.ts` L81–90 and `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` L224–233, but the Verification Log records no command or output for any of these ranges (the `grep` row only establishes that the string "sweep" is absent). The ranges cannot be confirmed by a reader, and the "Verified sites" enumeration cannot be checked for completeness — no command shows that no other full `RondaConfig` literal exists. Add the exact command and its output for the config-literal enumeration (and for the workflow input mapping), or drop the line numbers.

findings.title: Campaign output JSONs are unlisted committed artifacts
findings.body: The campaign legs write committed files into `docs/testing/ronda/` (`sweep-off-extended.json`, `sweep-on-extended.json`, the original-fixture control pair, and the precision pair), and step 11 says the evidence document "is assembled from those files; no run is hand-transcribed". Yet the "Recorded artifacts" section lists only `sweep-categories.json`, `sweep-effect-evidence.md` and `sweep-real-pr-evidence.md`; the rollback risk entry lists only `sweep-categories.json` plus fixtures and the changelog fragment; and Documentation Updates never mentions them. Name each output file (path and which run set it holds) in "Recorded artifacts", the withdrawal entry, and the runbook's Test Data table, so the committed artifact set is decidable.

findings.title: Benchmark output shape cannot satisfy AC9's per-finding attribution
findings.body: The record carries "the per-category pass record (every category with `produced_findings`/`produced_none` plus the uncategorized count, reuse of the step-3 `SweepPassRecord` type, not a parallel shape)". AC9 requires each sweep-on unexpected finding on the precision fixtures to be attributed "to the category (or categories, or uncategorized) recorded for it", and Smoke Step 9 repeats that. With two or more categories reporting `produced_findings` and more than one finding, an aggregate outcome set plus a single uncategorized count cannot say which finding came from which category. Add a per-finding category mapping to the benchmark output (Produced by the same `classifyFindings` result) or the precision evidence AC9 requires cannot be produced.

findings.title: AC17's gate-declaration path is left unplanned
findings.body: AC17 requires documentation to state both that the seeded benchmark is not a regression gate until the AC12/AC13 seeds exist and that the operator may declare the extended fixture ready to serve as the basis of a regression gate, with the declaration recorded (Use Case 5). This item (and the runbook's Step 12/assertions checklist) reduce AC17 to the "not a gate" statement plus "what a restored gate rejects is a deferred decision", so the declaration itself — who records it, in which artifact, and what it says — has no planned home and is untestable. Add the declaration's location and wording to this documentation item and a corresponding runbook assertion.

findings.title: Spec-fixed category list lacks the binding-enumeration marker
findings.body: The five categories are fixed by AC6 ("The swept list holds exactly the five categories in Statuses / Enum Values") and restated here and in the Seed Data row at line 144, but neither line carries the exact literal `**Binding enumeration**`. Per the review checklist an unmarked enumeration is indicative and may be satisfied by a coverage-equivalent set at implementation time, which would not meet AC6. Put the marker on the line that introduces the list.

findings.title: Fixture seed row mixes in category-list `matchTerms`
findings.body: This row gives a benchmark fixture seed "`matchTerms` over 'head', 'api', 'evidence'/'inference'", but `matchTerms` is defined as a field of the category-list artifact ("drawn from the category's `failureShape` wording"), and `api`/`evidence` do not appear in `pr-head-push-order`'s recorded failure shape. No step adds a `matchTerms` field to the fixture manifest, so the row either invents an unplanned manifest field or garbles the reference to the category list. Say which, and keep the seed rows limited to the fields the fixture manifest actually carries (`harderThan`, scenario, path).

findings.title: Documentation items are conditional and undecidable
findings.body: Two items leave it to the implementer to decide whether the work exists: "index the new runbook and evidence artifacts if that file's conventions require it" and "add the sweep mode ... only if those docs enumerate every review mode; verify against their current content during implementation". Nothing in the plan or a verify step settles the outcome, so completeness of documentation updates cannot be reviewed. Replace each with a decidable instruction (inspect the file, then record the resulting change or an explicit "no change needed because ..." outcome).

errorMessage: Model response was empty or whitespace-only
Model response was empty or whitespace-only

findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log and its matrix preflight row
findings.body: The PR has no description, so the required `Document Quality Gate` log is missing entirely. This spec adds a normative decision-gate consistency matrix plus several stateful contracts (per-category pass outcomes, the evidence-tier state machine, terminal adjudication outcomes), so the log must also carry a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary, or a reasoned not-applicable. With no log there is no evidence the matrix was audited, which the checklist treats as blocking before `ready-for-human-review`. Add the log to the PR description.

findings.title: Resolve cohort members that can never reach terminal adjudication
findings.body: The real-PR gate closes the eligible cohort before adjudication and requires that `every pull request in it must reach a terminal adjudication before the count is read` (also AC15(b) and the evidence-tier transitions, which say a reviewed-but-unadjudicated eligible pull request `blocks the transition rather than merely not counting`). Three cases defined here can never reach one: (a) membership does not require a recorded external review, yet `a pull request with no external review recorded is not adjudicated, whether or not it carried findings`; (b) a finding whose `unclear` outcome never resolves is said to mean the pull request `does not count`, which cannot be squared with the completeness rule; (c) an all-clean head where human adjudication records a defect outside the sweep's claim is neither a clean result (a defect was recorded) nor eligible for the terminal miss record (which requires a defect `within the sweep's claim`). One such pull request makes the ten-count and `real_pr_measured` unreachable forever, and no exclusion or escape is defined (for example, limiting cohort membership at the cutoff to heads that already carry a recorded same-head external review). Define the resolution and make `does not count` and the completeness rule agree.

findings.title: Exempt the pre-review skips from Use Case 1's postconditions
findings.body: The first postcondition states `Every category on the current list was considered for that head`, carving out only a pass that completes review execution and a pass that fails terminally after reaching it. AC1 says the opposite for the pre-review skips: a draft pull request or an automatic run that finds the head's existing check run `considers no categories and emits no per-category record, no sweep-activation statement, and no sweep metadata of any kind; it is not a sweep pass`. A draft head is one of the `normal review triggers` this use case's own preconditions allow, so its postconditions are unsatisfiable as written. Add the pre-review-skip carve-out to step 2, step 3 and postconditions 1, 3 and 4.

findings.title: Reconcile AC1's blanket both-surfaces claim with its write-failure case
findings.body: AC1 first states that for a pass that `completes review execution and publishes a review, that write is a check run whose outcome is a review, so the record is on both surfaces`. Later in the same criterion it states that when the review is already public and there was `a success check-run write that fails after its bounded retry`, the pass's `check run is therefore the success outcome the pass reached, or none at all where the write never landed`, and its record is on the logs `with whatever per-category surface its own check-run write actually produced`. Publishing a review therefore does not guarantee the check-run record, contradicting the earlier sentence, and the matrix row's `Reached completion with a check run whose outcome is a review` branch inherits the ambiguity. State one rule.

findings.title: Correct the Matrix 'Mirror surfaces' citations
findings.body: The `Mirror surfaces` citations point at the wrong sites, so the table's own requirement that `the prose sites named under Mirror surfaces state the same rule and must not contradict this table` cannot be verified. The enablement row cites a Business rule `Whether the sweep is enabled is read from the effective operator configuration value` (~106); that text is a Use Case 1 consideration and no Business Rule states it. The readability row cites Business rule `If the current category list cannot be read…` (~120) — the actual business rule is the later bullet beginning `When the sweep is enabled and the current category list cannot be read` — and names `Use Case 1 step 2`, which is the every-category sweep; the readability rule is in Use Case 1's Considerations. The pass-outcome row cites `the per-category pass record business rule (~541)`, which is the bullet beginning `The per-category pass record is carried on the surfaces AC1 assigns`. Refresh all three pointers.

findings.title: Put the pass outcomes and did-not-run records in Statuses / Enum Values
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values fixes code values and display labels for sweep categories, adjudication outcomes, the terminal miss record and the evidence tier, and states that this is the only site that fixes those values. The operator-visible per-category pass outcomes (`produced findings`, `produced none`, and `not determined`, which AC1 calls `the third per-category outcome`) and the sweep-did-not-run / unrecognized-enablement records have no entry there: they exist only as prose in AC1, AC18, AC19 and Operational Visibility, and `sweep-did-not-run` is written in kebab-case while every other new code value is snake_case (`ronda_only`, `ronda_rejected`, `sweep_enabled_miss`, `real_pr_measured`). Implementers must otherwise invent the values and labels for surfaces operators read. Add rows (code value, display label, description) or state that these are free-form display strings only.

findings.title: Say whether the descriptive miss record is admissible at `real_pr_provisional`
findings.body: The `real_pr_provisional` row says findings `are indicative only, support no effect claim, and are labeled as such`, while the claim-admissibility matrix row says `Descriptive real-pull-request claim: permitted at real_pr_measured alone`. Use Case 6's postcondition (`Real-pull-request evidence is read only as a descriptive record…`) carries no tier qualifier, and its step 4 reports the sweep-enabled miss record only after promotion. An operator cannot tell whether the descriptive sweep-enabled miss record may be published while the tier is provisional. Make the tier row and the matrix agree.

findings.title: Define the cost comparison AC11 requires
findings.body: AC11 (mirrored by the cost business rule and Use Case 4's postcondition) requires per-pass model calls and elapsed time to be `compared against the recorded per-pull-request convergence figures`, while Use Case 4 states the 2026-09-23 baseline `contains no Ronda pass cost at all … so the sweep-off control run is the only same-shape cost comparison available, and the per-pull-request figures give it context`. As written the mandated comparison has no defined content and no way to be shown done or not done. Either drop `compares them against` and require the per-pass figures to be reported alongside the baseline for context, or state exactly what is compared and against which figure.

findings.title: Disambiguate the 'review request' that defines a reached category
findings.body: AC1 defines a reached category as one that `the review request the pass issued carried`, adding that `the sweep composes that one request from the recorded list`, and elsewhere in the same criterion names `a failure of the review publication call itself`. If the request is the model request, a pass that fails before issuing any model request records nothing even though it reached review execution, contradicting Use Case 1's postcondition that every sweep pass reaching review execution records per-category outcomes. If it is the GitHub create-review call, a pass whose model call fails has reached no categories and records nothing, contradicting AC1's own `its logs carry the per-category record for the categories it reached`. Name the request, and state what a pass records when none was issued.

findings.title: Remove the duplicated 'used.' in AC9
findings.body: The preceding sentence ends `…and the effective review configuration the runs used.` and the next line begins `used. It reports unexpected findings per configuration`. Delete the stray fragment.

findings.title: Remove the orphaned sentence in the claim-admissibility row
findings.body: The Example cell of the claim-admissibility matrix row ends with a completed sentence (`…so a reported subset of the attempts does not admit the claim.`) followed by the dangling fragment `they do not pair the claim.`. It reads as an editing residue; delete it or fold it into the sentence it was cut from.

findings.title: Add the missing Document Quality Gate log with a Matrix coherence preflight row
findings.body: The PR has no description, so it carries no `Document Quality Gate` log. The checklist requires a current log on spec PRs, and because this spec adds five decision gates (the Decision-gate consistency matrix) and several stateful constructs (evidence-tier transitions, adjudication outcomes, per-category pass outcomes), the log must also carry a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary. Add the log and that row; without it the PR cannot proceed to `ready-for-human-review`, even though the in-document consistency matrix is present.

findings.title: Define the outcome recorded when human adjudication finds a within-claim defect no reviewer reported
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values → Adjudication outcomes says it is "the only site that fixes these code values" and adds only `ronda_only` and `ronda_rejected`. Yet Use Case 6 step 1, the real-pull-request business rule, and AC15(b) require that a pull request whose compared reviewers all reported no findings but whose human adjudication records a within-claim defect none of them reported is "terminally adjudicated only when that recorded defect is recorded as a confirmed miss for both the sweep-enabled review and the external reviewer, a terminal miss record". No code value, display label, or record shape is defined for that state. It is not a compared finding, so no finding-level outcome (including the dependency's `ronda_miss`, which attaches to a finding another reviewer or human reported) can carry it. This record gates the ten-pull-request count, the tier transition, and the confirmed-defect denominator, so engineering must invent it. Add the outcome (code value, display label, terminal status, and which record carries it).

findings.title: Make the precision-evidence pairing testable for real-pull-request recall claims
findings.body: The Claim admissibility matrix requires, for a recall claim, "the paired precision evidence on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count — and on the same category-list version, effective sweep configuration, and model identity as the real-pull-request comparison". A real-pull-request comparison has no fixture version and no benchmark sample count, so that condition cannot be satisfied or tested. AC15(d) and the precision business rule ("the same comparison must report unexpected findings for both configurations, on the same category-list version, effective sweep configuration, and model identity as the comparison the claim is made over") carry the same unclarity about whether the precision arms must match each other or the claimed heads. State the pairing explicitly: which properties a real-PR recall claim shares with its precision evidence (category-list version, effective sweep configuration, model identity), and that target, fixture version, and sample count bind only the two precision arms (AC9).

findings.title: Define whether passes that publish no review count as sweep-enabled reviews
findings.body: The business rule defines a "sweep-enabled review" as "a review whose pass actually ran the sweep and reported a category list version as used", and the ten-pull-request count and tier promotions ("the first sweep-enabled real pull request review is recorded") depend on it. But AC1 gives a pass that reaches review execution and is superseded before publication — or that publishes and then fails terminally — a full per-category record and logs the list version, while AC3 denies it any review summary. Whether such a head "carried a sweep-enabled review" and counts is therefore undefined. To compound it, Use Case 6 step 1 adds a qualifier the other sites do not use: "whose pass completed by a recorded cutoff", while the business rule, AC15(b), and the matrix say only "carried a sweep-enabled review ... up to a recorded cutoff". Define eligibility by pass outcome (review published or not) and say whether superseded and terminally-failed passes count toward the ten.

findings.title: Give the closed cohort a recovery path when it can never reach ten counted pull requests
findings.body: The cohort rules define no way out of a blocked cohort. The cutoff must be fixed "before any eligible pass's findings are visible", the cohort is every sweep-enabled review up to that cutoff, and every pull request in it "must reach a terminal adjudication before the count is read" (Use Case 6 step 1, the real-pull-request business rule, AC15(b), the Evidence-tier and Claim-admissibility matrix rows). A pull request with no external review recorded is never adjudicated, and an `unclear` adjudication is not terminal, so one such eligible pull request pins the tier at `real_pr_provisional` indefinitely. The operator cannot extend the cutoff (findings are already visible) and cannot bound a new cohort after the already-observed heads (that is the "subset" the spec forbids). A cohort that simply yields fewer than ten eligible pull requests has the same problem. State the remedy — for example a new prospective cutoff window that excludes already-observed heads under the same list version, or explicit handling of unadjudicable eligible pull requests.

findings.title: Define how confirmed-defect membership disagreement is resolved
findings.body: AC15(d) requires sweep-claim membership to be decided "against the recorded category list rather than after the fact", recorded "before the claim is read", and asserts that "two adjudicators reading the same closed cohort derive the same membership, since a defect either matches a recorded category or does not". Membership is a semantic match of a defect against a category's description and failure shape (for example `external-output-parsing`: "items are lost, merged, or misclassified"), and the spec gives no tie-break, no rule for an arguable match, and no way to record adjudicator disagreement — an `unclear` outcome is non-terminal, so it would block the count rather than settle membership. Either define a deterministic matching procedure with a disagreement rule, or drop the determinism claim and say how disagreement is recorded, since the denominator cannot otherwise be fixed before the recall figure is read.

findings.title: Cite the rule that actually defines the existing-check automatic skip
findings.body: AC1 lists the pre-review skips as "a draft pull request, or an automatic run that finds the head's existing check run, AC2", and AC19 also attributes that skip to AC2. AC2 defines only draft-skip and supersede behavior ("a skipped draft pass, or a pass superseded before publication"); it never mentions the existing-check skip. Cite the criterion that defines this skip, or define it here, so both pre-review skip cases rest on a stated rule rather than an absent reference.

findings.title: Correct the decision-gate matrix mirror-surface pointers
findings.body: Two mirror-surface pointers do not point at the rule they claim. The "Sweep enablement resolution" row cites `Business rule "Whether the sweep is enabled is read from the effective operator configuration value" (~106)`, but that text is a Use Case 1 consideration and the Business Rules section contains no enablement-resolution rule at all. The "Category list readability" row cites "Use Case 1 step 2", which is about considering categories, not list readability (that rule lives in Use Case 1 Considerations and in the Business Rules). Fix the pointers, and consider promoting the enablement-resolution rule to the Business Rules section so the matrix has a normative mirror.

findings.title: Reword the default-off rule to match deployment-wide webhook scope
findings.body: The business rule "This feature ships the sweep off unless a repository enables it (AC18)" conflicts with AC18, which scopes enablement per repository only for the Actions ingress and deployment-wide for the webhook, and with Out of Scope's exclusion of "a repository-keyed sweep enablement source for the webhook". Reword it as "unless the deployment's operator configuration enables it" so the default-off statement does not imply the excluded per-repository webhook control.
