findings.title: Add the per-rule Plan authoring rigor outcome record
findings.body: Neither the plan nor the (empty) PR description carries the per-rule outcome record the checklist requires: each of the six canonical rules (Rule 1 — Sampling an external output distribution; Rule 2 — One normative statement per fact; Rule 3 — Counts of codebase artifacts; Rule 4 — Independent verification of existence claims; Rule 5 — Expectations at the composed call site; Rule 6 — A conditional obligation names its scope) needs an outcome label (`Satisfied`, `Not applicable`, `Unsatisfied`) with its rationale, evidence, and revision SHA, linked to `plan-authoring-rigor-rules.md`. Group H treats a missing outcome record as blocking. Multiple rules plainly fire here — Rule 4 on existence claims such as "the `redactForbiddenValues` path already exists" and "`ChatCompletionResponse` drops the response's `model` field", Rule 3 on the enumerated caller/test-double counts in Implementation Order step 6, Rule 6 on the conditional obligations in Documentation Updates — so those outcomes must be recorded, not implied.

findings.title: Degraded-record boundary contradicts AC1/AC18/AC19 and the plan's own matrix row
findings.body: `src/core/run-review-pass.ts` rules 1–2 move the record-owing boundary from the changed-files read to the review request: "a pass that dies between the two — an authoritative-document fetch or any other GitHub error raised after `readChangedFiles` and before `deps.model.complete` — reached nothing and owes no sweep record at all, not even a degraded one". AC1 draws that boundary explicitly at the changed-files read: the pre-execution set it excludes is "a missing model credential, a config load error, or a deadline abort or GitHub error raised before the changed files are read", and a pass that "reaches review execution and then fails terminally — a model or GitHub error raised after the changed files are read" must carry its record on the logs. AC18/AC19 make the degraded records owed by any pass "that reaches review execution", and AC18 calls the unrecognized record "the only addition" over the same non-sweep outcome. Only the *category-reached* rule (reached = carried by the issued request) is spec-supported; the plan's use of it to suppress the degraded records is not. The plan also contradicts itself: the `## Decision-gate matrix` row "Pass-outcome surface assignment" still says "Terminal failure after review execution: record on logs", while rule 1's own definition of review execution is "reading the changed files **and** running the review". Testing Strategy scenario 5, the runbook's Step 4 second assertion and Step 5 case 3 ("emits no `sweep-did-not-run` ... no sweep metadata on any surface") and the Code Samples comment all encode the contradictory rule, so the whole boundary needs one decision that matches AC1/AC19 before approval.

findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log with the Matrix coherence preflight row
findings.body: The PR has no description, so it carries no `Document Quality Gate` log; the checklist makes a missing log important by default. The plan also contains a stateful contract — the `## Decision-gate matrix (plan-time classification)` with five gate rows and precedence rules for enablement resolution — so the log must include a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned `Not applicable`. A row reading `Not applicable — no stateful contract` would be a blocking misclassification here, so state the audit explicitly rather than omitting the log.

findings.title: Correct the stale Implementation Order step references
findings.body: Several cross-references point at the wrong step after the fixture-snapshot step was inserted, so an implementer following them lands in the wrong place: (a) this `src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts` bullet says the three CLI flags are "specified in Implementation Order step 10", but step 10 is "Fixture seeds" and the driver extension is step 11; (b) the Seed Data row "Original-thirteen fixture snapshot" says the snapshot is taken "before step 9 mutates the live fixture", but step 9 is "Workflow + example config" and the mutation is step 10 — the same row family in Implementation Order step 11 correctly calls it "the step-10 snapshot"; (c) Implementation Order step 11 says "The evidence doc (step 11) is assembled from those files", but the evidence document is assembled in step 12; (d) the smoke-test runbook's Step 8 says the original-thirteen snapshot is "created in implementation step 9" (should be step 10). Renumber all references against the final 17-step order.

findings.title: Parser-risk addendum misclassifies the matchers this plan adds
findings.body: `### Parser-risk addendum` says "Not applicable — the plan adds no lint/parser/scanner module and no regex-driven structured-text scanning", yet the plan specifies two matchers in the same document: Testing Strategy scenario 7's credential-shape scanner ("walks every seed and every committed evidence/fixture file ... fails if any value matches a real-credential shape (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `ghs_…`, a JWTs three-dot form, a `Bearer <token>` authorization value, or any `authorization`/`token`/... -named field carrying a non-placeholder value") and `run-review-pass.ts` rule 3's substring classifier over `title + "\n" + body`. Either classify these as in scope and supply parser-risk completeness (concrete edge-case enumeration, a named unit test file with at least one automated test per enumerated case, suppression semantics if suppressions are part of the feature) or remove the claim that no scanning exists. Note also that "non-placeholder value" is undefined, so the AC14 assertion cannot be implemented or reviewed as written.

findings.title: Verification Log does not verify the model-client seam the plan depends on
findings.body: `## Verification Log` records checks for `load-config.ts`, the workflow, `summary.ts`, the benchmark runner surface, the baseline docs and the cost baseline, but none for the claims this bullet builds its argument on: that `ModelClient` carries only `modelName`, that `complete` returns content alone, that `ChatCompletionResponse` drops the response's `model` field, that "every `complete` caller (`run-review-pass.ts`, `recall-benchmark.ts` ×2, `durability-regression.ts`, `webhook-job.ts`) ... destructures `.content`", and the line references used here and in Implementation Order step 6 (`src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts:475-489`, `src/cli/review-pr.ts` L81–90, `src/webhook/webhook-job.ts` L224–233, `tests/unit/cli/recall-benchmark.test.ts` L26/L243, `tests/unit/webhook/webhook-job.test.ts` L111, `tests/integration/review-pass.test.ts` L84/L223/L304). The existence claim for `redactForbiddenValues` (Testing Strategy scenario 7, Risks table) is likewise unrecorded. Per the technical-accuracy rule, add Verification Log rows for these surfaces or mark each claim "unverified — implementer must confirm before proceeding"; as written, step 6's return-shape break cannot be checked by reading.

findings.title: Define the finding fields the classifier depends on
findings.body: Rule 3 requires `classifyFindings` to "normalize each finding to lowercase `title + "\n" + body`", and AC20's guarantee (every published finding appears in the record against a category or as uncategorized) rests entirely on that mapping. The plan never verifies that parsed findings actually carry `title` and `body` strings (`src/inference/parse-model-response.ts` is explicitly "not modified" and appears in no Verification Log check), and it defines no behaviour for a finding with a missing, empty, or non-string `title`/`body` — the implementer must guess whether such a finding is uncategorized, throws, or is normalized from other fields. Name the exact fields of the parsed finding, add a Verification Log check that they exist, and state the fallback so the AC20 assertion is testable.

findings.title: AC14 scan covers only the benchmark tree, not all evidence artifacts
findings.body: Testing Strategy scenario 7 scopes the executable AC14 assertion to "every seed and every committed evidence/fixture file under the benchmark tree", but AC14 governs all "quality evidence produced by this feature" — which includes `docs/testing/ronda/sweep-effect-evidence.md`, `docs/testing/ronda/sweep-real-pr-evidence.md`, `docs/testing/ronda/sweep-categories.json` and the campaign output JSONs written by runbook Steps 8–9. As specified, the test would pass while a real credential sat in the evidence documents. Extend the scan's roots to `docs/testing/ronda/` (or state why the docs are out of scope and how they are otherwise checked), and do the same in the runbook's seed-presence step so the smoke test and the unit test agree.

findings.title: Decide whether the campaign output JSONs are committed artifacts
findings.body: Runbook Steps 8–9 write `docs/testing/ronda/sweep-{off,on}-{extended,original-thirteen,precision}.json`, and Implementation Order step 12 says the evidence document is "assembled from those files; no run is hand-transcribed", which only holds if the files survive. Yet `### Recorded artifacts (data layer equivalent)` lists exactly three new files (the category list and two evidence documents), and the Risks table's reversal lever removes only `docs/testing/ronda/sweep-categories.json` and the seeds. State whether the per-run JSON files are committed: if they are, enumerate them as recorded artifacts, add them to the revert lever, and index them in Documentation Updates; if they are transient, say what proves the evidence doc's figures and drop the "no hand-transcription" guarantee that the plan cannot then support.

findings.title: SweepCategory declares a `version` field nothing populates
findings.body: The types bullet defines `SweepCategory` as "(identifier, display label, description, failure shape, evidence source, count, version, `matchTerms: string[]`)", but the recorded-artifact bullet for `docs/testing/ronda/sweep-categories.json` puts `version` only at the list level (`SweepCategoryList` = version + categories) and lists no per-category version. Drop `version` from `SweepCategory`, or say what the per-category version means and who writes it.

findings.title: Documentation obligations are left conditional on an unstated check
findings.body: Three Documentation Updates items defer the decision to implementation without naming a check the implementer can perform: "index the new runbook and evidence artifacts if that file's conventions require it", "add the sweep mode ... only if those docs enumerate every review mode; verify against their current content during implementation", and AGENTS.md "no change expected ... unless the developer adds a `benchmark:sweep` script". Resolve each to a yes/no at plan time (or state the exact condition that flips it) so the reader can tell whether the update is owed.

findings.title: Add the Plan-Authoring Rigor outcome record
findings.body: REVIEW.md's plan-authoring-rigor backstop requires this plan's per-rule outcome record for Rules 1–6 at the recorded revision, and Group H makes a missing outcome record blocking. The document contains none: no rule is marked `Satisfied`, `Not applicable` or `Unsatisfied`, and no `def04bd`-derived evidence is recorded anywhere outside the Verification Log. At least Rule 1 fires (`classifyFindings` depends on the wording of model-produced finding text), Rule 3 and Rule 4 fire (the 13-seed count and the `grep -rn "sweep" src/ | wc -l` = 0 existence claim), and Rule 5 fires (`ModelClient.complete` has five consumers). Add the outcome record with per-rule evidence or a reasoned `Not applicable`.

findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log to the PR description
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the PR carries no `Document Quality Gate` log; REVIEW.md makes a missing log an important finding by default. findings.title: Reconcile where the `default` value comes from
findings.body: `## Summary` (line 10) describes the vocabulary as `on/off/1/0/true/false` — 'same ... as durability mode, plus an explicit `default` alias for `off`' — which makes `default` a sweep-only addition. The Verification Log row `Existing on/off vocabulary` (line 32) says `default` is 'recognized (durability only)', i.e. `parseDurabilityMode` already accepts it. Spec AC18 requires the sweep to accept the same values the durability switch already accepts, so one statement is wrong: either `default` is existing vocabulary (and 'plus' is misleading) or the sweep invents a value durability does not accept (contradicting AC18). State which parser accepts `default` today and align both sites and the runbook's Step 3 expectations.

findings.body: This line says the `original-thirteen` snapshot is 'created in implementation step 9 by copying `manifest.json` and `patches.json`', but the plan creates it in step 10 (Fixture seeds); step 9 is the workflow/example-config change. The plan has the mirror error: line 225 says 'The evidence doc (step 11) is assembled from those files', while the evidence campaign that writes `sweep-effect-evidence.md` is step 12. findings.title: State how the recall and control legs run inference
findings.body: The three campaign legs give the extended-fixture and original-thirteen commands only `--sweep-mode`, `--runs` and `--output-file`, and add `--quality` only to the precision leg — while the same paragraph says a run must call the model and that 'the real-model precision campaign must run inference (`--quality` alone ...)'. If `--quality` is the inference switch (as the runbook's Step 9, lines 280 and 294, also assumes), the AC8 recall/variance legs run without a model call and record no model identity, which contradicts AC8's per-run recall plus immutable model version requirement. Either add `--quality` to the recall and control commands or name the flag that makes them call the model.

findings.title: Verify the code-surface claims and the benchmark CLI contract
findings.body: The Verification Log rows at lines 31–34 (`Existing on/off vocabulary`, `Review summary / check-run renderers`, `Benchmark runner surface`, `Operator config precedence surface`) record file paths rather than a query, so the behavioural claims resting on them are not reproducible, and the plan's line-number citations (`src/cli/recall-benchmark.ts:475-489`, `ronda-review.yml` L134–145, L81–90, L224–233, L84/L223/L304, L26, L243, L111) are not checked by any recorded command (REVIEW.md: numeric cross-references that cannot be confirmed are an important finding). The benchmark row also never verifies the flags the campaign depends on: the plan adds only `--sweep-mode`, `--runs` and `--output-file`, yet the runbook uses `--manifest` and `--patches` (runbook lines 213–226) and asserts the semantics of `--quality` and `--precision-response-file`. Record a runnable query for each, or mark the flag contract 'unverified — implementer must confirm before proceeding'.

findings.title: Correct the AC1 assertion line
findings.body: The Assertions Checklist's AC1 line says 'terminal failures after the request record `not_determined` on the logs only'. That contradicts AC1, which reserves `not_determined` for a failure that precedes the review result and requires the ordinary `produced_findings`/`produced_none` values where the review is already public (`reviewPublished` guard or a failed post-publication check-run write), exactly as this runbook's own Step 6 says at lines 173–178. Restate both cases so the checklist does not certify the wrong behaviour.

findings.title: Make the documentation obligations executable
findings.body: Three of the five Documentation Updates bullets are conditional with no scope or owner: line 163 'index the new runbook and evidence artifacts if that file's conventions require it', line 164 'no change expected (... unless the developer adds a `benchmark:sweep` script — then list it ...)', and line 165 'add the sweep mode ... only if those docs enumerate every review mode; verify against their current content during implementation'. These match REVIEW.md's vague-wording pattern ('update as needed') and leave an implementer unable to tell whether the work is done. Decide each now (required or not, with the file and section named).

findings.title: Plan the AC15(d) membership recording
findings.body: Spec AC15(d) requires every membership decision — each compared finding's and every defect only human adjudication records — to be recorded in the cohort's evidence before a claim is read. The `sweep-real-pr-evidence.md` bullet lists the tier label, the count, the caveat, the adjudication-outcome application record, cohort mechanics, the terminal-miss record and the tier transitions, but never the per-finding match against a swept category, and the `Claim admissibility` matrix row (line 139) does not list it as a claim input either. Add it to the record's required contents so the comparative-claim gate the plan defines is checkable.

findings.title: Complete the evidence-document content lists (AC9, AC17)
findings.body: Step 12's content list for `sweep-effect-evidence.md` requires only 'the precision regression result'. AC9 additionally requires the committed evidence to report unexpected findings per configuration, attribute each sweep-on unexpected finding to its category/categories/uncategorized, report sweep-off findings as unattributed, and report each precision fixture's clean/not-clean status per configuration; those appear only in the runbook's Step 9 at run time, not in the artifact the plan defines. Separately, the AC17 statement (line 166, and runbook line 347) omits AC17's second clause — that the operator may declare the extended fixture ready to serve as a gate basis, with the declaration recorded. Plan both into the artifact.

findings.title: Drop the 'no residue on any pull request' claim
findings.body: The withdrawal row ends 'Neither lever touches the published review or check run: the sweep writes only metadata, so a withdrawn sweep leaves no residue on any pull request.' That contradicts the plan's own surfaces: AC3 puts the sweep activation and list version in the published review summary, and AC1 puts the per-category record on the check-run output, so every pass published while the sweep was on leaves that metadata on the pull request permanently. The levers write nothing new; they cannot remove what was already published. Reword to 'the withdrawal writes nothing new to existing pull requests' and acknowledge the already-published metadata.

findings.title: Bound false attribution in `classifyFindings`
findings.body: Rule 3 decides each category's outcome by lowercase literal substring hits over `title + "\n" + body`, using `matchTerms` 'drawn from the category's `failureShape` wording' (line 60); a short term such as `head` (used by the state-reconstruction seed's terms at line 148) matches `header`, so a category can be recorded `produced_findings` for text it did not produce, and Testing Strategy scenario 2 only asserts case-insensitivity, multi-match and determinism. The Parser-risk addendum (line 121) then calls this 'model-adjacent record-keeping, not text scanning', which misdescribes a literal scanner over model-produced free text. State the specificity requirement for `matchTerms` (and test a non-matching look-alike), or restate the addendum so the scanning risk is acknowledged.

findings.title: Mark the five-category enumeration as binding
findings.body: This bullet enumerates the five swept categories (`pr-head-push-order`, `credential-pattern-gap`, `external-output-parsing`, `record-identity`, `guard-fails-open`) and Testing Strategy scenario 8 (line 113) asserts 'the swept list holds exactly the five required categories', so the enumeration is meant as binding — but no `**Binding enumeration**` marker appears on or immediately above the line that introduces it, so by REVIEW.md's rule it is only indicative and may be satisfied by a coverage-equivalent set. Add the marker where the enumeration is introduced.

findings.title: Disambiguate `matchTerms`
findings.body: `matchTerms` names the sweep list's classifier field (lines 60, 68, 71), the Seed Data table uses 'matchTerms over "head", "api", "evidence"/"inference"' for a benchmark seed's matching metadata, and step 10 calls the existing manifest shape `matchTermGroups` (line 220). Three names spanning two artifacts for the same word invites implementing or asserting the wrong field. Use distinct names.

findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required `Document Quality Gate` log is missing. findings.title: Define the terminal miss record and fix the vacuous terminal rule
findings.body: Use Case 6 and the real-pull-request business rule require a head whose compared reviewers all reported nothing but whose adjudication records a defect to be "terminally adjudicated only when that recorded defect is recorded as a confirmed miss for both the sweep-enabled review and the external reviewer, a terminal miss record". That record has no code value, display label, or row anywhere, while `Statuses / Enum Values → Adjudication outcomes` declares itself "the only site that fixes these code values" — so an implementer must invent the outcome. Worse, AC15(b) defines terminal as "every compared finding carries `ronda_miss`, `ronda_better`, `duplicate`, or a Ronda-only outcome ... or the clean result `clean_agreement` is confirmed"; a head with no compared findings satisfies that vacuously, contradicting the "only when" clause. Define the terminal miss record as a first-class outcome and make the terminal rule require it explicitly.

findings.title: Specify how a sweep-off control run is produced
findings.body: The matched control is required by AC15(d) for every comparative real-PR claim, but the only description of producing one is a Use Case 6 consideration: "a sweep-off review of the same pull request heads ... recorded but not published". No step, precondition, or AC covers it. It also collides with the existing flow: AC1 makes "an automatic run that finds the head's existing check run" a pre-review skip, and AC2 allows exactly one published review per head SHA — so a control on a head that already carries its sweep-enabled review is either skipped or a second review. State the control run's trigger, how it avoids publication and the existing-check skip, and the surface its results are recorded on, and add an AC for it.

findings.title: Define cohort succession and scope the cohort cutoff
findings.body: Use Case 6, AC15(b), the real-PR business rule, and the tier matrix all close the cohort at "a recorded cutoff fixed in advance, before any eligible pass's findings are visible", and every member must be terminally adjudicated before the count is read. Nothing says a closed cohort may be succeeded by a new cohort with a new cutoff, so a cohort that closes with fewer than ten counted pull requests appears to strand the tier at `real_pr_provisional` forever. The visibility bound is also unscoped (the cohort's own passes, or any sweep-enabled pass ever), and read literally it forbids ever fixing a second cutoff once the first findings are public. Define when a new cohort may be opened and which passes bound its cutoff.

findings.title: Make category membership testable instead of asserting objectivity
findings.body: AC15(d) claims "two adjudicators reading the same closed cohort derive the same membership, since a defect either matches a recorded category or does not", and the whole no-post-hoc-selection safeguard rests on that. But membership is decided by matching a defect against prose descriptions and failure shapes (AC4), and nothing in AC4/AC6 makes that matching deterministic. Either state a testable matching rule the adjudication must record (the fields it must fill, and what happens when more than one category matches) or soften the claim and the safeguard that depends on it.

findings.title: Resolve whether a rejected review request was issued
findings.body: AC1 defines a category as reached when "the review request the pass issued carried it", and says "a pass that fails before issuing any review request has reached none". It also lists "a model credential the model API rejects" among post-execution failures whose logs carry the per-category record (and the pass-outcome matrix example likewise presupposes a record). A request rejected at authentication sits exactly on the boundary: depending on whether it counts as issued, the record is empty or records every category as not determined. State which side a rejected or unauthorized request falls on, and whether an empty per-category record is emitted at all.

findings.title: Define 'a check run whose outcome is a review'
findings.body: AC1 and the `Pass-outcome surface assignment (AC1)` gate row make the record's surface depend on "a check run whose outcome is a review", a term never defined (check runs have conclusions such as success or failure). AC1 then says a post-publication failure's "check run is therefore the success outcome the pass reached ... and in either case its per-category record is on the logs ... with whatever per-category surface its own check-run write actually produced", which reads both as logs-only and as possibly carrying the record. Define the term and reconcile the two statements so implementers know which write carries the per-category output.

findings.title: Fix the empty-value-means-off contradiction
findings.body: Use Case 1 says "An absent, empty, or whitespace-only value means off, with no record, and counts as not supplied". Those two halves conflict: "counts as not supplied" means the value defers, and AC18 plus the enablement gate's own example say an empty value at a higher-precedence source "defers to the next source", so a lower-precedence recognized on value makes the effective result on, not off. Reword to say an empty value supplies nothing and the sweep is off only when no source supplies a recognized on value.

findings.title: Define the cost comparison against the per-PR figures
findings.body: AC11 and O7 require the cost evidence to be "compare[d] ... against the recorded per-pull-request convergence figures", but Use Case 4 states that "the 2026-09-23 cost baseline contains no Ronda pass cost at all" and that the per-pull-request figures only "give it context". No metric, unit, or expected relation is defined for a per-pass versus per-pull-request comparison, so AC11 cannot be verified. Either define the comparison and what result would be meaningful, or record the baseline figures as context alongside the sweep-on/sweep-off figures and drop the comparative requirement.

findings.title: Back the Use Case 2 'what would change it' postcondition with a field
findings.body: Use Case 2's postcondition promises that "Any reader can tell why each category is on the list and what evidence would justify changing it", but the Information shown list, the initial category table, AC4, AC6, and AC7 contain no per-category field for what evidence would justify a change. Either add that field to the recorded-list requirements (AC4/AC6) or drop the promise from the postcondition so the artifact and the acceptance criteria agree.

findings.title: Correct the matrix's mirror-surface pointers
findings.body: The `Sweep enablement resolution (AC18)` row cites `Business rule "Whether the sweep is enabled is read from the effective operator configuration value" (~106)`, but that text is a Use Case 1 consideration (around line 120), not a Business Rules bullet — Business Rules has no enablement-resolution rule. The next row's `(~120)` likewise points into Use Case 1 rather than the list-readability business rule. Fix the pointers and prefer stable section/rule references over line numbers that drift.

findings.title: Disambiguate 'effect claim'
findings.body: The term is used broadly and narrowly. Use Case 6 says "No real-pull-request effect claim is published below the minimum count" but then defines a narrower "comparative effect"; AC15(a) forbids "effect claim[s]" below Real-PR evidence (measured); the tier table says provisional findings "support no effect claim". Because the tier and claim-admissibility rules make even descriptive real-PR claims measured-only, define whether "effect claim" means any real-PR claim or only comparative ones, and use one phrase per meaning.

findings.title: State the recognized on/off values
findings.body: AC18 defers the exact accepted strings to "the plan" and by reference to "the same, case-insensitive, on and off vocabulary that Ronda's existing on/off operator switches ... already accept", yet the gate's third outcome — and its distinct recorded degradation — is exactly "non-empty and unrecognized". Without quoting the accepted set (or citing the authoritative list), the recognized/unrecognized boundary cannot be tested from this document. State the values, or require the plan to cite the existing list explicitly.

findings.title: Define what baseline comparability means and the configuration it uses
findings.body: AC8 requires a repeated original-fixture comparison for "baseline comparability", then says it does not reproduce the baseline: "no run against it is classified as baseline reproduction", "the comparison is reported ... as a new original-fixture comparison under the configuration the run itself records, and no field of it is compared against the recorded alias". Use Case 3, the Business Rules and Coverage Matrix O5 additionally refer to "the recorded baseline-comparison configuration AC8 defines", which AC8 never defines. So what comparability is (comparison with the 2026-09-10 six-to-eight-of-thirteen figures, or only sweep-on versus sweep-off on the original fixture) is left to the implementer, and the run cannot in fact be compared with the baseline it is named after. Define the configuration artifact by name and state exactly what is compared against the 2026-09-10 figures, or state that the original-fixture run is a new baseline and comparability with the old figures is not claimed.

findings.title: Define how a closed cohort that cannot reach ten is resolved
findings.body: Use Case 6 step 1 and AC15(b) close the eligible cohort at a cutoff fixed before any eligible pass's findings are visible, and require every member to be terminally adjudicated before the count is read. The spec never says what happens when that closed cohort contains fewer than ten eligible pull requests, nor when a member can never be adjudicated: Business Rules say "a pull request with no external review recorded is not adjudicated", so one such member blocks the label permanently. Nothing permits opening a further cohort for the same list version (the only stated restart is "Revising the list restarts that count"), so Real-PR evidence (measured) can become unreachable for a list version. Use Case 6's action "Keep accumulating reviewed pull requests" also implies the count grows after closure, which the cutoff forbids. Define how a cohort is completed, extended, or replaced, and how an unresolvable member is excluded without outcome-aware selection.

findings.title: Say whether a sweep-enabled review must be published
findings.body: Business Rules define a "sweep-enabled review" as "a review whose pass actually ran the sweep and reported a category list version as used", and Operational Visibility says the logs record "that the sweep ran, the list version". A pass superseded before publication runs the sweep and logs the version but publishes no review at all (AC1, AC2), so by that definition it is a "sweep-enabled review" even though no review exists. That matters because the first such pass promotes Fixture evidence only to Real-PR evidence (provisional) and the term also governs the counted cohort. Require publication (AC3's review summary) in the definition, or state explicitly that a superseded pass promotes the tier.

findings.title: Resolve whether a descriptive real-PR claim is allowed at provisional tier
findings.body: Use Case 6's postcondition says "Real-pull-request evidence is read only as a descriptive record of what sweep-enabled reviews caught and missed", which allows a descriptive reading at any real-PR tier including provisional. The claim-admissibility matrix says "Descriptive real-pull-request claim: permitted at `real_pr_measured` alone", and the real-pull-request business rule says that even at ten "only a descriptive sweep-enabled miss record may be claimed". Three sites disagree on whether a descriptive miss record may be published below ten counted pull requests. Pick one rule and make Use Case 6, the business rule, and the matrix row state it identically.

findings.title: Define who applies the within-claim match and how disagreement is resolved
findings.body: The membership rule calls itself "the objective match", says "no recorded entry decides membership — a record states the test's verdict, and a run's entry recording a membership the test contradicts is a misrecording that carries no membership", and concludes "two adjudicators reading the same closed cohort derive the same membership, since a defect either matches a recorded category or does not". The only stated test is matching against each category's prose failure shapes (AC4); no matching procedure, arbiter, or tie-break is given, and no artifact can demonstrate that a membership was decided before the recall figure. As written the determinism claim does not hold and the requirement (repeated in AC15(d) and the claim-admissibility gate) cannot be verified. Name who applies the match, how a contested or misrecorded membership is corrected, and soften or remove the determinism sentence.

findings.title: Say whether refreshing a finding-instance count creates a new list version
findings.body: AC4 and AC19 require every category to carry a finding-instance count, and AC7 says "The recorded list carries a version and a revision history entry for each change". Nothing states whether updating a category's count as new real-pull-request evidence arrives counts as a change. If it does, every count refresh yields a new version, and AC15(c) and the tier transitions then demote Real-PR evidence (measured) to provisional and restart the ten-pull-request count — a heavy side effect the spec never discusses and never gives the operator an option to avoid. State whether counts are part of the versioned content, and if they are, that a count refresh restarts the count.

findings.title: Separate the sweep-did-not-run record from the unrecognized-enablement record
findings.body: Operational Visibility says "A sweep-did-not-run record ... states that the sweep did not run because its category list was unreadable, empty, or malformed (AC19), or that a non-empty enablement value was unrecognized (AC18)". But AC18 makes an unrecognized value off: the pass runs as an ordinary non-sweep review whose only addition is the enablement record, and the enablement matrix row says every off outcome "records no per-category pass result", with the unrecognized case recording only the unrecognized value. One term therefore names two different records, one of which is not a sweep pass at all. Give them distinct names here.

findings.title: Add sweep-did-not-run to Statuses / Enum Values or drop the token
findings.body: The category list readability row, normative per the matrix introduction, requires the pass to "record `sweep-did-not-run`", an opaque code value. Statuses / Enum Values has no such entry, display label, or description; AC19 only requires recording "that the sweep did not run"; and the unrecognized-enablement record has no code value at all, so the two records are specified at inconsistent precision. Since Statuses / Enum Values is the site that fixes code values and display labels, either define `sweep-did-not-run` (and a code value for the unrecognized-enablement record) there or remove the token from the matrix and describe the record in prose.

findings.title: Refresh the matrix's mirror-surface references
findings.body: The matrix row cites a "Business rule" at ~106 and ~120 for text that actually lives in Use Case 1 → Considerations (the enablement-resolution and list-degradation bullets), and cites ~541 for the per-category pass record business rule, which in this draft is in the Business Rules section far from that line. Because the matrix is the normative summary and requires mirror sites to "state the same rule and must not contradict this table", stale pointers send a fixer to the wrong place. Reference section names (or `AC` numbers) instead of approximate line numbers, and correct the "Business rule" label.

findings.title: Reconcile the single composed request with the multiplied-model-calls question
findings.body: AC1 fixes the sweep as composing "that one request from the recorded list" and defines a reached category by what "the review request the pass issued carried", while O7 and AC11 ask whether the sweep "multiplies model calls per pass" and measure model calls per pass as if multiple calls were possible. If the sweep is by construction one composed request, the multi-call question has only one answer and AC11's metric premise is misleading; if it is not, the reached-category rule is under-specified for a pass that issues several calls. Either state that the sweep adds no model call by construction, or define reached-ness per call.

findings.title: Replace "manufactured finding" with something checkable
findings.body: AC10 requires that a pass "produces no manufactured finding for any category", and the Business Rules add that Ronda "must never be required, encouraged, or rewarded for producing at least one finding per category". Neither defines "manufactured" nor how it is detected, so the criterion cannot be tested as written. The observable the spec already has is the Use Case 4 precision test (unexpected findings on fixtures that expect a clean result); state the criterion in those terms.

findings.title: Fix the enablement scope wording
findings.body: The Business Rules say "This feature ships the sweep off unless a repository enables it (AC18)", but AC18 and Use Case 1 scope enablement to "one deployment's effective configuration": per repository only where the Actions ingress supplies it, and deployment-wide where the webhook resolves one process-wide value for every repository it serves (a repository-keyed source is Out of Scope). Phrase it as "unless the deployment's operator configuration enables it" so the business rule does not promise per-repository control the webhook ingress does not have.

findings.title: Define an exit for cohort pull requests that can never be terminally adjudicated
findings.body: Use Case 6 step 1 and the real-pull-request business rule require the eligible cohort to be closed before adjudication and every pull request in it to reach a terminal adjudication, yet they also state that a pull request with no recorded external review "is not adjudicated" and that an `unclear` outcome is not terminal because it needs more human review. Nothing defines how such a pull request ever leaves the closed cohort, so one eligible pull request with no external review, or one `unclear` finding, blocks the count and every real-PR claim indefinitely; the only remaining move, moving the recorded cutoff to exclude that pull request, is exactly the favorable-case selection the closed-cohort rule forbids. Define a terminal disposition (for example, excluded from the cohort by rule with the reason recorded, or a resolution deadline) so `real_pr_measured` is reachable without cohort cherry-picking.

findings.title: Add the missing Document Quality Gate log with a Matrix coherence preflight row
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required `Document Quality Gate` log is absent; a missing log is an important finding by default. This spec contains a stateful contract (the decision-gate consistency matrix and the evidence-tier transitions), so once the log is added it must carry a `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned `Not applicable`; a bare "no stateful contract" claim would be a blocking misclassification. Add the log before requesting human review.

findings.title: Reconcile the measured-tier label with the cohort-completeness requirement
findings.body: AC15(b) assigns `Real-PR evidence (measured)` only when the closed cohort has every pull request terminally adjudicated, and the claim-admissibility matrix repeats that condition. The Evidence tier `Valid transitions` list says a measured label demotes only when the counted pull requests fall below ten and that a measured tier with ten or more counted pull requests and no revision "stays Real-PR evidence (measured)". If a sweep-off control recorded on a counted head reopens that head's adjudication while the count remains ten or more, the label is simultaneously forbidden by AC15(b)/the matrix and required to persist by the transitions list. State which rule governs and add the missing demotion trigger.

findings.title: Add the precision-regression gate to the decision-gate consistency matrix
findings.body: The matrix states "This feature adds four decision gates and one pass-outcome rule" and its rows cover enablement, list readability, pass-outcome surfaces, tier transitions, and claim admissibility. The precision-regression decision in Use Case 4 and AC9 is a further gate: it has defined inputs (unexpected findings and per-fixture clean status for both configurations), two allowed outcomes (regressed / not regressed), required next actions (record the regression and revise or narrow the list, or accept), mirror sites, and it gates the later default flip under the business rules. Add it as a matrix row, or state why it is not a workflow decision gate.

findings.title: Reconcile AC1's single-request "reached" rule with the open model-call question
findings.body: AC1 defines the categories "reached" by a failed pass as those "the review request the pass issued carried", and fixes that "the sweep composes that one request from the recorded list". That is a technical design constraint on the model interaction and it settles by construction a question the evidence requirements leave open: Use Case 4, O7 and AC11 require measuring "whether the sweep multiplies model calls per pass", which cannot happen if every pass issues exactly one composed request. Either define "reached" without the one-request assumption, or state that model calls are fixed by design and drop the multiplication question from the cost evidence.

findings.title: Require the adjudication record to carry the matched swept category
findings.body: AC15(d) and the real-pull-request business rule require the recall denominator's membership to be recorded by "the adjudication that adjudicates it naming the swept category the defect it records matches", and the claim-admissibility matrix makes that recorded membership a condition of admissibility. No acceptance criterion, Operational Visibility item, or Statuses / Enum Values field requires the adjudication record to capture the matched category (the adjudication-outcomes table defines only outcome code values and labels). As written the membership decision has no defined storage, so every real-PR recall claim is inadmissible; add an AC and a visibility item for the category-match field.

findings.title: State what the paired precision evidence must match for a real-PR recall claim
findings.body: AC15(d) and the claim-admissibility matrix require "the paired precision evidence AC9 defines on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count". The clause never says what those must be the same as. Read against the claimed heads it is unsatisfiable, because real pull-request heads have no fixture version or sample count; read against AC8's benchmark comparison it sits oddly inside a real-PR claim. State that the precision evidence is the AC8/AC9 benchmark precision comparison whose category-list version, effective sweep configuration, and model identity match the claimed heads, which is what Use Case 4 and the O6 note actually require.

findings.title: Correct the mirror-surface citations in the decision-gate matrix
findings.body: The matrix's Mirror surfaces column cites "Business rule 'Whether the sweep is enabled is read from the effective operator configuration value' (~106)" and "Use Case 1 step 1". That text exists only as a Use Case 1 consideration (it begins near line 120), the Business Rules section has no enablement-resolution rule, and Use Case 1 step 1 only starts a pass. The list-readability row similarly cites "Use Case 1 step 2", which does not state that rule. Point these cells at the real mirror sites (Use Case 1 Considerations, AC18/AC19, and the list-readability business rule) so the matrix identifies the prose it claims to summarize.

findings.title: Define the per-category record states and `sweep-did-not-run` in Statuses / Enum Values
findings.body: The matrix writes the literal `sweep-did-not-run` and the spec uses "produced findings", "produced none" and **not determined** as per-category record states, but none of them appears in Statuses / Enum Values, which supplies display labels and allowed values for every other new code value (`ronda_only`, `ronda_rejected`, the three tiers). Add the record states there with their labels, or stop presenting `sweep-did-not-run` as a code value, so implementers do not have to invent the check-run and log field values.

findings.title: Define or correct the "existing check run" pre-review skip cited from AC2
findings.body: AC1, AC18, AC19 and the sweep-did-not-run business rule treat "an automatic run that finds the head's existing check run" as a pre-review skip and cite AC2 for it. AC2 defines only the draft skip and supersede behavior; this document never states the existing-check-run skip or where it comes from, yet that skip decides whether any sweep metadata is emitted. Define the skip here or cite the dependency spec that owns it.

findings.title: Scope AC6 so it does not freeze the revisable category list
findings.body: AC6 requires the swept list to hold "exactly the five categories in Statuses / Enum Values" and the excluded entries to be exactly the four named themes, while Use Case 2, AC7 and the Statuses note that spec-AC-compliance "may be added at a later list revision" explicitly allow revisions that add or remove categories. As written AC6 becomes false the first time a revision is applied. Scope it to the initial delivered list version (or the list as of this feature's release) so it does not contradict the revision mechanism.

findings.title: Give the recall denominator and membership rule one normative site
findings.body: The confirmed-defect denominator and membership rule is stated almost verbatim in five places: AC15(d), the real-pull-request business rule, the Coverage Matrix O11 note, the claim-admissibility matrix Inputs cell, and the `real_pr_measured` enum row. The spec already establishes a single-owner pattern for the pass-outcome rule ("AC1 (sole owner of this rule); every other site references AC1 rather than restating it"); apply the same pattern here, because several paraphrases of a rule this intricate will drift apart.
